## Overview

Build the challenge system that tracks recurring daily and weekly goals, grants XP, resets progress by period, and exposes current challenge progress to users.

Challenges should be separate from achievements. They are repeatable goals, not permanent badges.

## User Story

As a learner, I want daily and weekly challenges, so that I have short-term goals that reward regular learning activity.

## Goal

Users should be able to complete predefined and custom challenges based on application events.

Completed challenges should grant XP, respect configured caps, emit reward notifications, and reset according to their configured period.

## Main User Flow

A user performs an action that matches an active challenge, such as logging in, completing a lesson, completing a quiz, posting in course chat, or receiving likes.

From there, the system should:

- Update the user's challenge progress for the current period.
- Check whether the challenge requirement is completed.
- Enforce max completions and XP caps for the period.
- Grant XP when a challenge is completed.
- Store the challenge completion.
- Emit a WebSocket reward notification.
- Allow the frontend to refetch challenge progress through REST APIs.

## Challenge Progress

Challenge progress should be scoped by:

- Tenant
- User
- Challenge
- Reset period

Supported reset periods:

- Daily
- Weekly
- Monthly

Progress should reset automatically based on the configured period.

Completed challenges can repeat in later periods.

## Predefined Challenges

Predefined challenges should be seeded per tenant as part of the challenge system.

Examples of predefined daily challenges:

- Daily login
- Complete one lesson today
- Complete one quiz today
- Post one course chat message today

Examples of predefined weekly challenges:

- Complete five lessons this week
- Complete three quizzes this week
- Finish one course this week
- Be active five days this week
- Receive three likes this week

Admins should be able to disable predefined challenges later, but disabling them should not remove historical completions or XP.

## Challenge Completion

When a challenge is completed, the system should:

- Create a challenge completion record.
- Create an XP transaction.
- Increase lifetime XP.
- Increase spendable XP.
- Trigger a reward notification.

Challenges should not create permanent achievement badges.

## Caps And Limits

Challenges should support:

- Max completions per period
- XP cap per period

These limits should prevent users from earning more XP than the challenge configuration allows for the current period.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Challenge progress is tracked per user and period.
- Daily challenges reset daily.
- Weekly challenges reset weekly.
- Predefined challenges are seeded per tenant.
- Challenge progress is updated from gamification events.
- Completed challenges grant XP through XP transactions.
- Completed challenges increase lifetime XP.
- Completed challenges increase spendable XP.
- Challenge completions can repeat in later periods.
- Max completions per period are enforced.
- XP caps per period are enforced.
- Challenge completion emits a WebSocket reward event.
- Challenge progress is available through user-facing APIs.
- Duplicate events do not duplicate challenge completion or XP.
- Challenges do not create permanent achievement badges.
title: Build Challenge System

body:
> Track: AI-agents-for-research · generative materials
> Difficulty: advanced (comfortable reading ML papers and modifying PyTorch/JAX)
> Compute: one GPU per team is enough for the week

## Overview

A pretrained generative model of crystals already knows chemistry: give it a formula and it returns plausible structures. But plausible is not useful — out of the box it reproduces the average of its training set, with no notion that you want a crystal that frequency-doubles a UV laser, or one as light as possible without falling apart.

This is where GPT was before RLHF, and the fix is the same: reinforcement-fine-tune the generator against a reward that encodes what you want. Your task this week is to do that for crystals, using three ingredients:

1. a **generative model** — CrystalFormer (the policy)
2. a **reward model** — a property or stability predictor
3. **reinforcement learning** — PPO/GRPO to close the loop

Pick one of two starter hunts, or bring your own target:

- Track A — deep-UV nonlinear-optical crystals
- Track B — ultralight stable solids
- Track C — your own objective

## The method: RL fine-tuning, as in LLM alignment

Same recipe as aligning an LLM — sample, score, reinforce — with a KL leash to the base model so the policy stays fluent.

| | Aligning an LLM | This challenge |
|---|---|---|
| Policy | pretrained LLM | pretrained CrystalFormer (`space group → Wyckoff → atoms → coords → lattice`) |
| Data | internet text | ~1.4 M known crystals (Alexandria / Materials Project) |
| Reward | learned (human preferences) or exact (code/math checker) | learned (property predictor) or exact (symmetry, density) |
| Algorithm | PPO / GRPO | PPO / GRPO (in the repo) |
| Target | helpful, harmless | stable and on-target property |
| Failure mode | reward hacking | reward hacking |

The loop, from Cao & Wang ([arXiv:2504.02367](https://arxiv.org/abs/2504.02367), Fig. 1a) — sample from CrystalFormer, score with a reward model, update by RL, repeat:

![Reinforcement fine-tuning workflow: CrystalFormer (policy p_θ) samples crystal structures, a reward model r(x) scores them, and an RL update improves the policy. From Cao & Wang, arXiv:2504.02367, Fig. 1a.](https://arxiv.org/html/2504.02367v1/x1.png)

The objective is the paper's:

> ℒ = 𝔼[ r(x) − τ · ln( p_θ(x) / p_base(x) ) ]

Maximize reward without drifting far from the pretrained model; the τ term is the KL leash.

A reward can be *learned* (a property predictor — flexible but hackable) or *exact* (symmetry, density — cheap and unfakeable). Both starter tracks are anchored by something exact — symmetry in Track A (enforced at generation), density in Track B — so a hit can be verified without expensive DFT.

## Background

- CrystalFormer (Cao & Wang, IOP CAS, with the Lü Jian group at Jilin University; *Science Bulletin* 2025 — [news](https://www.iop.cas.cn/xwzx/kydt/202510/t20251022_7994908.html), [code](https://github.com/deepmodeling/CrystalFormer)) generates in the symmetry-reduced Wyckoff representation, so the space group is an explicit token you can steer. That is why the symmetry-based targets below fit so naturally.
- Reinforcement Fine-Tuning for Materials Design (Cao & Wang, [arXiv:2504.02367](https://arxiv.org/abs/2504.02367)) is the direct predecessor: property models as rewards, joint optimization of competing properties (e.g. dielectric constant and band gap). Read it first.
- The repo already ships PPO/DPO/REINFORCE, an end-to-end sampling → relaxation → stability pipeline, and reward factories. You extend a working system, not build from scratch.

## Tracks

Tracks A and B are worked examples, ready to run; Track C invites your own objective. Comparing tracks, or combining properties, makes for a strong submission.

### Track A — deep-UV nonlinear-optical crystals

NLO crystals frequency-double lasers; deep-UV ones (e.g. the borate KBBF) are rare and strategically important. Second-harmonic generation is forbidden in any centrosymmetric crystal, so the core requirement is a non-centrosymmetric space group. CrystalFormer emits the space group as its first token, so you get this by construction — condition generation on non-centrosymmetric groups rather than filtering after the fact. Stability and band gap then drive the reward, and spglib confirms the symmetry survives relaxation:

| Ingredient | What it enforces | How | Role |
|---|---|---|---|
| non-centrosymmetric space group | SHG is symmetry-allowed | condition CrystalFormer's space-group token; verify with spglib after relaxation | constraint (by construction) |
| stability (E-hull) | the crystal could exist | MLFF relax + energy-above-hull (in repo) | reward — exact (MLFF) |
| wide band gap | UV transparency | a band-gap predictor (yours to provide) | reward — learned |
| large SHG coefficient (stretch) | it is actually a good NLO crystal | DFT on the top candidates | verify-only |

Reward = stability × gap-in-window, over structures generated directly in non-centrosymmetric space groups. Fine-tune to raise the yield of stable, wide-gap candidates, then validate the best.

### Track B — ultralight stable solids

What is the lightest thermodynamically stable crystal? Density is exact (mass / cell volume) and stability is the MLFF E-hull you already have — no learned model needed, so the reward is fully verifiable.

| Reward term | What it enforces | How it's computed | Reward type |
|---|---|---|---|
| low mass density | lightness | mass / cell volume | exact |
| stability (E-hull) | it won't collapse | MLFF relax + energy-above-hull (in repo) | exact (MLFF) |

Reward = f(1/density) with a stability penalty. The interest is the tension: low density favors open frameworks, stability punishes them. Map and push the density-vs-stability Pareto front.

### Track C — your own objective

The recipe is general — thermoelectrics, transparent conductors, high-refractive-index optics, auxetics, ferroelectrics, and more are all fair game. A good self-chosen target meets three bars:

- useful — a real application to point at;
- cheap to score — seconds per candidate (fast predictor, empirical formula, or exact check), since RL needs thousands of evaluations and per-sample DFT is too slow as a reward;
- verifiable — a crisp way to confirm a hit (exact if possible, else a higher-fidelity model or DFT on the top candidates).

Clear those bars and go; check with the organizers early.

## Getting started

Works end-to-end today:

- Pipeline: `postprocess.sh` runs sample → convert → MLFF-relax → energy-above-hull (ORB-v3 by default). This is your evaluator.
- RL: `crystalformer/cli/train_ppo.py` drives PPO with rewards (`--reward {ehull,prop,dielectric,force}`), exploration knobs (`--sg_temperature`, `--sg_epsilon`, `--exploration_weight`, `--diversity_weight`), a KL penalty (`--beta`), and entropy (`--alpha`). DPO and classifier-guided generation are also available.
- Rewards: `crystalformer/reinforce/reward.py` has `make_ehull_reward_fn` (stability), `make_prop_reward_fn` (scalar → target), and `make_dielectric_reward_fn` (dielectric × gap). Use the dielectric one as a worked reference for wiring in a property model, and `make_prop_reward_fn` as the scaffold for your own.

Your build:

- Track A: generate directly in non-centrosymmetric space groups — fix one with `--spacegroup`, or mask CrystalFormer's space-group distribution to the non-centrosymmetric subset — and reward stability × band gap. The band-gap predictor is yours to provide (a pretrained MEGNet/MatGL/matminer model, or a light one trained on Materials Project gaps). Use spglib post-relaxation to confirm the symmetry holds.
- Track B: add a density term — no external model needed; the work is reward shaping and the stability trade-off.

The reward model is part of the challenge, not a given: it is what separates a real discovery from a hallucinated one.

## Deliverables

Bounded for a week, with a tail that can become a paper. A submission can be a research study, an agentic tool, or both.

Research study — the RL fine-tuning experiment:

1. A reproducible RL fine-tuning run: documented reward (terms, weights, rationale), training config, reward curves, and a sanity check that the reward scores known materials correctly.
2. A before/after result: sample from the base and tuned models; report the shift in the verifiable metric with error bars over several seeds.
   - Track A: fraction of samples that are non-centrosymmetric, stable, and in the gap window.
   - Track B: density distribution and lowest density at fixed stability.
3. Validated candidates: exact check on all samples; DFT relaxation + property on the top finalists; a table of the best (formula, space group, E-hull, property), marking rediscoveries versus novel.
4. A short report/notebook and a pull request, including one honest **reward-hacking** story — how the policy cheated, how you caught it, what you did.

Agentic framework — a human-in-the-loop design tool for experimentalists:

- takes a target stated in plain language and turns it into a reward/constraint spec;
- orchestrates the loop — generation, scoring, optional RL fine-tuning, validation — and returns candidate structures with provenance, stability and property estimates, and the reasoning behind each pick;
- builds on the repo's MCP server (`mcp/csp_mcp.py`, which exposes `generate_structures`): wrap the pipeline steps as agent tools behind a clean interface.

Deliver the working tool, a short recorded design session, and notes on reliability — above all, how it avoids handing an experimentalist hallucinated or unstable candidates.

## Judging

- Correctness and reproducibility of the RL loop.
- Rigor of the before/after (real baselines and error bars).
- Depth of validation.
- Insight into reward hacking and the exploration–exploitation trade-off.
- Clarity.

Bonus: rediscovering a known target material, a validated novel candidate, or a clean multi-property Pareto analysis.

## Reward hacking

The part that makes it research. The policy will find the cracks in your reward, as LLMs learn to flatter a flawed preference model: structures scored high-gap because they fall outside the predictor's training distribution; collapse to a single high-reward template; "stable-looking" structures the force field rejects. Detecting and defending — held-out DFT checks, reward-model ensembles or uncertainty penalties, diversity metrics, tuning the KL leash — is the science. This is why both starter tracks anchor on something exact — symmetry (enforced at generation in Track A) and density (Track B) cannot be hallucinated.

## Research extensions

- Better RL: GRPO, or risk-sensitive GRPO — does risk-seeking surface rarer, better candidates?
- Multi-objective: a real Pareto front (A: symmetry × gap × SHG; B: density × stability × a mechanical constraint), as with dielectric × gap in the paper.
- More symmetry-defined targets: ferroelectrics/piezoelectrics (polar groups), chiral crystals (Sohncke groups) — all exact to check with spglib.
- Robust rewards: ensembles, uncertainty penalties, active learning from DFT feedback.
- Generalization: fine-tune on one chemical system, test transfer to unseen elements.

## Resources

- CrystalFormer: https://github.com/deepmodeling/CrystalFormer
- RL fine-tuning paper (read first): https://arxiv.org/abs/2504.02367
- CrystalFormer background: https://www.iop.cas.cn/xwzx/kydt/202510/t20251022_7994908.html
- ML force fields: ORB / MACE / MatGL (`train_ppo.py --mlff_model`)
- Symmetry and analysis: spglib, pymatgen, matminer
- Concepts: RL fine-tuning of LLMs (RLHF / RLVR); PPO/GRPO; energy-above-hull; second-harmonic generation and non-centrosymmetric point groups

## Overview

Build an admin-facing challenge configuration area where admins can create and manage custom daily and weekly challenges.

This should extend the challenge system with configurable challenge definitions based on supported application events.

## User Story

As an admin, I want to create custom recurring challenges, so that I can encourage learners toward specific daily or weekly behaviors.

## Goal

Admins should be able to create, edit, disable, and review custom challenges with reset periods, event requirements, XP rewards, caps, and event-specific filters.

Custom challenges should use the same runtime processing as predefined challenges.

## Main User Flow

An admin opens challenge configuration and sees existing predefined and custom challenges.

From there, they can:

- Create a new custom challenge.
- Open and edit an existing custom challenge.
- Disable a challenge that should stop granting progress.
- See which challenges are active or disabled.
- See whether a challenge is daily or weekly.
- Review XP rewards, caps, and configured requirements.

When creating or editing a challenge, the admin should be able to:

- Set the challenge name and description.
- Choose daily or weekly reset.
- Select an application event.
- Choose the requirement type.
- Configure event-specific filters.
- Set the requirement value.
- Set the XP reward.
- Set max completions per period.
- Set XP cap per period.
- Save the challenge as active or disabled.

## Challenge Configuration

Supported reset periods:

- Daily
- Weekly
- Monthly

Supported requirement types:

- Count-based
- Time-window based

Each challenge should support:

- Name
- Description
- Status
- Reset period
- Selected app event
- Requirement type
- Requirement value
- XP reward
- Max completions per period
- XP cap per period
- Optional filters

## Event Filters

The builder should only expose filters that can be evaluated from the selected event payload.

For example:

- Course filters can be shown when the event includes a course ID.
- Score filters can be shown when the event includes a quiz score.
- Filters that cannot be evaluated from the selected event should not be available.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Admin can access challenge configuration.
- Admin can see predefined and custom challenges in one place.
- Admin can create a custom daily challenge.
- Admin can create a custom weekly challenge.
- Admin can edit a custom challenge.
- Admin can disable a challenge.
- Admin can select only supported application events.
- Admin can configure requirement type and requirement value.
- Admin can configure XP reward.
- Admin can configure max completions per period.
- Admin can configure XP cap per period.
- Admin can configure only filters supported by the selected event payload.
- Active custom challenges are processed by the challenge system.
- Disabled challenges stop granting new progress and XP.
- Disabling a challenge does not remove historical completions or XP.

## Overview

Build an optional reward shop where students can spend earned XP on rewards configured by admins.

The reward shop should be hidden behind a feature flag. When the feature flag is disabled, XP, achievements, challenges, levels, and leaderboards should continue working normally.

## User Story

As a student, I want to redeem my earned XP for rewards, so that gamification has a tangible benefit.

As an admin, I want to manage reward items and redemptions, so that my organization can offer internal or external rewards.

## Goal

Students should be able to browse active reward items and redeem them using spendable XP.

Admins should be able to manage reward items and manually fulfill reward redemptions.

Redeeming rewards should decrease spendable XP only. Lifetime XP should remain unchanged.

## Main User Flow

When the feature flag is enabled, a student opens the reward shop and sees available reward items.

From there, they can:

- See each item's XP cost.
- See whether they have enough spendable XP.
- Redeem an available item.
- Receive redemption confirmation.
- See their redemption history and redemption statuses.

When a student redeems an item, the backend should:

- Validate that the reward shop feature flag is enabled.
- Validate that the item is active and currently available.
- Validate quantity limits.
- Validate per-user redemption limits.
- Validate that the student has enough spendable XP.
- Create a reward redemption record.
- Create an XP spending transaction.
- Deduct spendable XP.
- Keep lifetime XP unchanged.

An admin can manage reward items and redemptions from the admin area.

## Feature Flag Behavior

When the reward shop feature flag is disabled:

- Students should not see reward shop UI.
- Student reward shop routes should not be accessible.
- Admins should not see reward shop management.
- Reward shop APIs should reject or hide reward shop functionality.
- Existing reward shop data should remain stored.
- XP earning, achievements, challenges, levels, and leaderboards should continue working.

## Reward Items

Reward items can represent in-app or external rewards.

Examples:

- Cafeteria coupon
- Company merch
- Extra learning material
- Event ticket
- Custom internal reward

Each reward item should support:

- Name
- Description
- Image or icon
- XP cost
- Status
- Quantity limit, optional
- Per-user redemption limit, optional
- Availability start date, optional
- Availability end date, optional
- Redemption instructions, optional

Disabled, expired, or unavailable reward items should not be visible or redeemable by students, but should remain visible to admins.

## Redemption Management

Reward redemptions should support these statuses:

- Pending
- Fulfilled
- Cancelled
- Rejected

For the first version, fulfillment can be manual.

Admins should be able to:

- View redemptions.
- Filter redemptions by status.
- Mark redemptions as fulfilled.
- Cancel or reject redemptions when needed.

Cancelled or rejected redemptions may refund spendable XP depending on the admin action.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Reward shop is hidden when the feature flag is disabled.
- Student reward shop routes are inaccessible when disabled.
- Admin reward shop management is hidden when disabled.
- Reward shop APIs reject or hide reward shop functionality when disabled.
- Existing reward shop data remains stored while disabled.
- Admin can create reward shop items when enabled.
- Admin can edit reward shop items.
- Admin can disable reward shop items.
- Admin can view active and disabled reward shop items.
- Student can view active and available reward items when enabled.
- Student cannot see disabled, expired, or unavailable reward items.
- Student can redeem an active item when they have enough spendable XP.
- Redemption enforces item status, availability, quantity limit, and per-user limit.
- Redemption creation and XP deduction happen atomically.
- Redemption creates a reward redemption record.
- Redemption creates an XP spending transaction.
- Redemption decreases spendable XP.
- Redemption does not decrease lifetime XP.
- Admin can view reward redemptions.
- Admin can filter redemptions by status.
- Admin can mark redemptions as fulfilled.
- Admin can cancel or reject redemptions.

## Proposition: Daily Challenges + Rewarded Bonus Fight

### Concept
Add two lightweight engagement systems:
1. **Daily Challenges** — 3 rotating objectives per day with exclusive loot rewards
2. **Bonus Fight via Rewarded Ad** — Watch a 30s ad to unlock +1 extra FIGHT beyond the daily 5

---

### Why It Fits Bitbrawler

| Aspect | Fit |
|--------|-----|
| **Session length** | Challenges add 1-2 min of goal-checking. Bonus fight adds 15s. Perfect for mobile. |
| **Retention hook** | Daily challenges create a reason to log in every day (not just when energy is full) |
| **Ad integration** | Non-invasive, opt-in, perfect for "watch ad for extra fight" — high completion rates |
| **Current gap** | No reason to play after 5 fights. Challenges give "one more thing to do". |

### Impact on Retention

| Metric | Expected Lift |
|--------|--------------|
| DAU/WAU | +20-30% (players logging in for daily challenges) |
| Avg fights/run | 4.87 → 5.5+ (bonus fight option) |
| D7 retention | +10-15% (daily objective habit formation) |

**Source**: Appsamurai 2026 — rewarded ads improve retention 3.5x; Gamelight — limited events boost D30 by 8-15pp.

---

### Design Details

#### Daily Challenges (3 rotating types)
1. **Brawler** — Win 3 fights today → Reward: Uncommon lootbox-tier item
2. **Survivor** — Take less than 100 total damage across all fights → Reward: XP boost consumable
3. **Collector** — Open today's lootbox → Reward: Small stat bonus consumable
4. **Streaker** — Maintain a 3-day lootbox streak → Reward: Epic lootbox-tier item
5. **Slayer** — Deal 500+ total damage today → Reward: Rare lootbox-tier item

Each day, pick 3 challenges at random. Completion grants a special **Challenge Token** exchangeable in a mini-shop.

#### Bonus Fight via Rewarded Ad
- After exhausting 5 daily fights, a "Watch Ad for +1 Fight" button appears
- Max 1 extra fight per day via ad
- The ad fight grants normal XP/loot
- Optional: Double rewards if player pays attention (ad verification)

#### Tech Requirements
- New DB table: `daily_challenges` (challenge_id, description, reward_type, active_date)
- New DB table: `player_challenge_progress` (player_id, challenge_id, progress, completed, date)
- New UI: `DailyChallengePanel.tsx` — compact widget on Arena page
- New UI: `ChallengeRewardModal.tsx` — reward claim animation
- Ad SDK integration for rewarded video (AdMob or similar)
- Config toggle for ad/non-ad mode (for testing/offline)

### Effort Estimate

| Area | Effort |
|------|--------|
| DB schema + Supabase setup | 1 day |
| Challenge system logic (generation, tracking, reset) | 2 days |
| Challenge UI (panel + rewards) | 2 days |
| Rewarded ad integration | 1 day |
| Tests + balance | 1 day |
| **Total** | **~7 days** |

**Effort Score**: 4/5

### Potential Risks
- Ad integration requires adding external SDK → affects build size
- Challenge rewards must be balanced to not unbalance the game economy
- Daily challenges reset needs to sync with existing daily reset at midnight Paris

---

### References
- [Segwise — Mobile Game Retention Strategies 2026](https://segwise.ai/blog/boost-mobile-game-retention-strategies) — Progressive reward systems lift D7 by 10-15%
- [Revlum — Limited Time Events Impact](https://revlum.com/academy/how-limited-time-events-impact-player-retention) — FOMO drives participation
- [AppsAmurai — Rewarded Ads 2026](https://appsamurai.com/blog/rewarded-ads-in-mobile-games/) — 60% of top grossing games use rewarded ads
- [Unity — Rewarded Video Best Practices](https://unity.com/blog/the-fundamentals-of-rewarded-video-ad-placements) — Design as part of game economy

Type: Proposition majeure

2. Challenges and rewards

Do not build training or partner referral in this phase. Those are Phase 3.

Goal:
Make CTVs feel progress, competition, and clear next targets every week/month.

Core principle:
All rankings and challenge completion must be based on valid eligible orders only. Cancelled, returned, refused, disputed, rejected, or outside-policy orders must not count.

--------------------------------------------------
PART 1: Leaderboards / Bảng xếp hạng
--------------------------------------------------

Routes:
- CTV: `/dashboard/bang-xep-hang`
- Admin: `/admin/leaderboards` if admin configuration is needed

Add CTV sidebar item:
- `Bảng xếp hạng`

Leaderboard tabs:
1. Top doanh thu tuần
2. Top số đơn tuần
3. Top doanh thu tháng
4. Top số đơn tháng
5. CTV mới nổi

Definitions:
- Revenue = eligible product revenue from valid attributed orders.
- Order count = valid attributed orders only.
- Current week should use Vietnam time. Prefer Monday to Sunday.
- Current month should use Vietnam time.
- `CTV mới nổi` should rank CTVs approved recently or CTVs with first valid orders recently. Keep it simple if needed: partners approved within last 30 days, ranked by valid order count/revenue.

CTV visibility:
- Show top 10 by default.
- Highlight current CTV row if they are in ranking.
- If current CTV is outside top 10, show their own rank separately if practical.
- Show explanation that cancelled/returned/refused orders do not count.

Admin visibility:
- Admin can view leaderboards with filters:
  - week
  - month
  - metric revenue/order count
  - partner type referral_ctv
- Admin can export later, but not required now.

Implementation options:
- First version can calculate leaderboard dynamically from PartnerOrder/PartnerCommissionLedger.
- If performance is poor later, add snapshot table. Do not overbuild now.

Suggested helper functions:
- getVietnamWeekRange(date)
- getVietnamMonthRange(date)
- getValidPartnerOrdersForRange(partnerType, start, end)
- getLeaderboard(metric, range, partnerType)

Valid order rules:
Exclude:
- cancelled orders
- returned/refunded orders
- refused orders
- rejected commission ledgers
- outside-policy discount orders if already marked rejected/on_hold
- orders with no valid partner attribution

Use existing cancellation exclusion helpers from Issue #34 if available.

Columns:

- Reward: configurable text/amount
- Purpose: activate new CTV

- Reward: unlock higher commission tier or bonus text
- Purpose: push monthly performance

- Reward: highest commission tier or bonus text

- Optional: if content usage logging exists. If no usage tracking exists, skip this challenge for now.

Do not reward only clicks or shares unless usage tracking and anti-abuse rules exist. Focus on valid orders first.

PartnerChallenge
- id
- title
- description
- challengeType: first_orders | monthly_orders | monthly_revenue | first_order_after_approval | custom
- status: draft | active | archived
- targetMetric: valid_order_count | valid_revenue

- rewardedAt nullable
- createdAt

Admin challenge page:

CTV challenge page:

  - Đang thực hiện

- Optional: create CTV notification/announcement-style item if a partner notification model exists.
- Optional: create admin notification if reward requires manual handling.

When a challenge reward needs manual payout:
- Create admin notification:
  `CTV hoàn thành thử thách cần xét thưởng`
- Link to `/admin/challenges` or partner detail.

Do not automatically create payout records unless reward workflow is already defined.

CTV menu after Phase 2:

- Lịch chương trình

- Bảng xếp hạng

Do not add Phase 3 items yet unless pages are useful.

--------------------------------------------------
PART 6: Timezone
--------------------------------------------------

All weekly/monthly windows should use Vietnam timezone.

- Week: Monday 00:00:00 to Sunday 23:59:59 Asia/Ho_Chi_Minh
- Month: first day 00:00:00 to last day 23:59:59 Asia/Ho_Chi_Minh

Store dates in UTC, display using vi-VN and Asia/Ho_Chi_Minh.

--------------------------------------------------
PART 7: SQL and migrations
--------------------------------------------------

Schema changes are expected for challenge models.

Leaderboard can be dynamic and may not need schema.

Include:
- Prisma migration
- manual Supabase SQL
- deploy/restart order

If using string status fields instead of Prisma enums, keep values consistent and documented.

PART 8: Acceptance criteria
--------------------------------------------------

Leaderboard:
- CTV can open `/dashboard/bang-xep-hang`.
- Shows top week/month by valid revenue and valid order count.
- Current CTV is highlighted if present.

Quality:

## Context

Parent initiative: #381 `[Tracker] Fair Rewards`

Related discussion: https://github.com/Usernode-Labs/flutter-mobile-app/discussions/440

Challenges are part of the Fair Rewards initiative. The Challenges screen should become an attention-routing surface for reward opportunities: what matters now, what is progressing, and what reward/status is attached.

The latest design direction is:

- organize active challenges into a few human-perceived time bands
- represent challenge work as atomic cards inside those bands
- keep the card itself focused on progress + reward/status
- keep challenge detail untouched for this iteration

## Problem

The current Challenges structure is too coarse and too flat. A plain active/completed/missed model does not explain urgency, campaign grouping, partial progress, pending verification, or long-running seasonal reward work.

At the same time, putting every concern inside each card makes the list noisy. Deadlines, campaign context, and urgency should mostly live at the group/band layer. The card should stay small and scannable.

Do not solve this by adding more status/date UI to the challenge detail page. The detail page can already carry task copy and CTA; this issue is about the layer above it.

## Product Model

Use **perceived-time bands**, not raw deadline sorting:

- `Featured`: the most relevant challenge for this user right now; not necessarily the nearest deadline
- `Today`: immediate attention; short-deadline or daily-cadence work
- `This Week`: near-term planning horizon
- `Season`: long-running/background/campaign work, including season-bounded block production and community challenges

Do not add a separate `Ongoing` band for MVP. If rewards settle within a season, background work still belongs under `Season`.

Complex challenges should be split into **atomic child challenges** where possible. The parent/campaign provides shared context and deadline; children carry the individual earning mechanics.

Example shape:

```text
Featured
[ Produce blocks this epoch ]

Today                                      5h left
[ Fill survey        0 / 1        500 pts ]

This Week                                  4d left
[ Give Kudos         2 / 5        400 / 1,500 pts ]
[ Propose change     Submitted    waiting review ]

Season                                     Ends Jun 30
[ Help members       Joined       waiting review ]
[ Block production   90% success  4,500 / 6,500 pts ]
```

## Atomic Card Scope

Each active challenge card should contain only:

- challenge title
- one compact reward/progress rail
- whole-card tap target
- no inline CTA

Task instructions, requirements, verification explanation, and CTAs remain on the existing challenge detail page, but changing that page is out of scope for this issue.

## Atomic Card Content Model

Each card should be driven by a small presentation model, not raw challenge data:

- `title`
- `leftText` for metric/progress/status, for example `0 / 1`, `2 / 5`, `Submitted`, `90% success`
- `rightText` for reward/status, for example `500 pts`, `400 / 1,500 pts`, `pending 500 pts`, `completed 500 pts`, `waiting review`
- `phase` for visual treatment
- `fill?` when a meaningful bounded metric exists
- optional `featured` treatment

`fill` should be nullable. `null` means state-only rail, not fake progress. When present, rendered fill must be clamped to `0..1`.

## Required Card States

Support only states we can justify from current/historical challenge behavior:

- `open`: user has not made progress yet
- `inProgress`: measurable progress exists but the challenge is not complete
- `pendingFinalization`: user action/metric is complete, but verification or final point assignment is still pending
- `completed`: final points have been assigned

Do not introduce a separate `needsAction` state for MVP. Historically we have not had challenges that require a submitted-work-changes-needed loop, so adding that state now would be speculative.

Important rule: **pending points should only appear when the challenge is awaiting finalization**, not merely while the user is making progress.

## Time And Urgency Rules

- Group headers carry shared deadline/urgency copy such as `5h left`, `4d left`, or `Ends Jun 30`.
- Cards should not repeat the group deadline by default.
- A card may show time only if it is standalone or has a materially different deadline than its group.
- `Featured` and urgent are different concepts. Featured means highest relevance; time bands communicate deadline pressure.

## Challenge Archetypes To Cover

Widgetbook scenarios should cover the historical challenge shapes we have seen:

- one-shot/binary: survey, set username, zkPassport
- counted action: give kudos, send transactions, use dApps
- threshold: cross a minimum value such as transaction count or block production threshold
- continuous/proportional: block production success rate where reward scales with performance
- economic outcome: reward depends on in-app result, such as opinion market balance
- quality judged: bug reports, help members, app improvement suggestions

Campaign-style examples such as dApp weeks or broader improvement programs should appear as grouped atomic child cards, not overloaded mega-cards.

## Implementation Notes

- Build reusable presentation widgets in the design system where they are genuinely reusable.
- Keep DS widgets presentation-only: no Riverpod, no FRB imports, no data fetching.
- Put band/status derivation in `lib/features/challenges/`, not the design system.
- Add Widgetbook v4 stories/scenarios for the banded active surface and atomic card states.
- Swap only the active Challenges list to the new banded surface.
- Keep completed/missed history behavior out of this issue unless needed to avoid regressions.
- Remove or stop using the older `ChallengeCardCompact` path for the active-card pilot.
- Do not modify `ChallengeDetailPage` except to fix a regression caused by the active-list change.

## Non-goals

- Challenge detail page redesign or added deadline/status strip
- Speculative `needsAction` / changes-requested challenge state
- Activity feed
- Profile earned-history IA
- dApp notification lifecycle
- leaderboard/topochain ordering changes
- full challenge grouping/campaign data model beyond the MVP presentation bridge
- real per-challenge enrichment APIs
- Widgetbook Cloud integration
- Marionette/debug tooling

## Acceptance Criteria

- Active Challenges are grouped into `Featured`, `Today`, `This Week`, and `Season` bands where data allows.
- No separate `Ongoing` band is introduced for MVP.
- No `needsAction` card state is introduced for MVP.
- Band headers show shared urgency/deadline copy when meaningful.
- Atomic cards render as title + single reward/progress rail only.
- The whole card is tappable and there is no inline CTA.
- Card rails do not duplicate shared band deadlines by default.
- Pending reward copy appears only for `pendingFinalization` states.
- Progress fill is nullable and clamped to `0..1` when rendered.
- Cards and band headers work in light and dark themes and on a narrow mobile viewport.
- Widgetbook v4 includes scenarios for the perceived-time bands and for binary, counted, threshold, continuous, economic, and judged challenge archetypes.
- Widget tests cover rendering, tap behavior, state labels, fill clamping, and basic band derivation.
- `ChallengeDetailPage` remains behaviorally and visually unchanged, aside from unrelated existing state.

## Test Plan

- `flutter analyze`
- `flutter test`
- `cd packages/ds_lints && dart run bin/lint.dart ../..`
- `cd widgetbook && dart run build_runner build -d`
- `cd widgetbook && flutter test`
- Manual Widgetbook check on Samsung Galaxy S20 viewport in light and dark themes

> Track: AI-agents-for-research · generative materials / inverse problems
> Difficulty: advanced (comfortable reading ML papers and modifying JAX)
> Compute: one GPU per team is enough for the week

## Overview

Point an X-ray source at an unknown powder and, in minutes, you get a diffraction pattern — a 1-D barcode of the 3-D atomic arrangement inside. Turning that barcode back into the actual crystal structure is one of the oldest and most useful inverse problems in science: it is how we find out **what we just made**. When a sample happens to yield a good single crystal, the structure falls out almost for free — but often it doesn't, and then the powder pattern is all you have. Reading a structure out of it has, for a century, demanded expert intuition and painstaking trial-and-error.

It is hard for a real reason. Single-crystal structure solution has been essentially routine since *direct methods* (Nobel Prize, 1985); powder is harder still — collapsing 3-D diffraction into a 1-D pattern overlaps the reflections, and it remains unsolved for complex structures. Very different structures can produce nearly identical patterns, so naively optimizing "make the simulated pattern match the data" wanders into a maze of look-alike wrong answers ([Segal et al., *Digital Discovery* 2026](https://arxiv.org/abs/2512.04036)).

Here is the bet of this challenge. A generative model that has already seen a million crystals **knows what real structures look like**. Give that knowledge to the solver as a *prior*, and the maze collapses — you search only over structures that are *both* consistent with the measured pattern *and* chemically plausible. Your job this week is to build that solver, and watch it read a structure straight out of an experiment.

## The idea

Three ingredients, one loop:

1. **a generative prior** — CrystalFormer, a pretrained transformer that samples plausible crystals. It emits the **space group first**, then Wyckoff sites, atom types, coordinates, and lattice.
2. **a forward simulator** — compute the powder pattern of any candidate structure and score how well it matches your target.
3. **reinforcement learning** — reward structures that fit, keep them close to the prior, repeat.

Formally, you minimize a **variational free energy**:

$$F \;=\; \underbrace{\mathbb{E}_{X\sim q(X)}\big[-r(X)\big]}_{\text{goodness of fit — "energy"}} \;+\; \tau\,\underbrace{\mathrm{KL}\big(q(X)\,\|\,p(X)\big)}_{\text{stay realistic — "entropy"}}$$

- $r(X)$ — how well the pattern **simulated** from structure $X$ matches the **measured** pattern.
- $p(X)$ — the pretrained **CrystalFormer** prior; the KL term is a leash keeping proposals on the manifold of real crystals.
- $q(X)$ — your solver, tuned to **one target pattern at a time**.

This is the **maximum-entropy principle with a learned prior**: fit the measurement, but stay as close as you can to what real crystals look like. It buys you two things that make the "impossible" problem tractable:

- **No gradients through the simulator.** The reward is just a number, so a fast, standard, non-differentiable simulator is fine — and the rough loss landscape that traps gradient descent is simply not in your path.
- **The symmetry is discovered, not assumed.** Because CrystalFormer samples the space group as its first token, you do **not** need to know it in advance — the solver proposes a space group and the pattern fit selects it.

It is a modern remake of a classic idea: Harris et al. (1994) solved structures from powder data by random-move Monte Carlo — propose a structure, score it against the pattern, accept or reject. We swap the random moves for a pretrained generative model that already knows chemistry, and the accept/reject for the variational free energy above.

## The reward $r(X)$

You know the **composition** — it is your sample. Condition CrystalFormer on that formula and let it sample structures (space group and all). For each candidate:

- **Simulate** its powder pattern with pymatgen's `XRDCalculator` (kinematic, fast), then convolve the discrete peaks with a profile (Gaussian / pseudo-Voigt) into a continuous curve.
- **Score** it with the **cosine similarity** to the target pattern — one clean number in $[0,1]$, and that is the reward.

Matching the broadening and $2\theta$ window to the target is where much of the real craft lives — a faithful fit metric matters more than the RL details.

## Do you need a database of patterns? No.

To solve a structure from a *given* pattern, all you need is a structure→pattern simulator for the fit; the prior is trained on **structures** (CIFs), not on paired pattern↔structure labels. So databases are only for scoring yourself:

- **Self-supervised recovery — start here.** Take a known crystal, simulate its pattern (add realistic broadening and noise), and see whether your solver recovers it. Unlimited targets from Materials Project / COD CIFs, ground truth included.
- **Benchmark** on held-out cases from **SimXRD-4M** (4M simulated patterns; [arXiv:2406.15469](https://arxiv.org/abs/2406.15469)); report structure-match rate.
- **Stretch to real data** with experimental patterns from **opXRD** ([arXiv:2503.05577](https://arxiv.org/abs/2503.05577)), where background, texture, and broadening break simulator-clean assumptions — exactly where the prior earns its keep.

## Getting started

Repo: [`deepmodeling/CrystalFormer`](https://github.com/deepmodeling/CrystalFormer) (**JAX**). You are reusing a working system — you write one new reward function, not a new algorithm. (It is the very same RL loop as the sibling challenge #65; only the reward is new.)

- **Add a reward:** `make_xrd_reward_fn` in `crystalformer/reinforce/reward.py`, next to `make_prop_reward_fn`. It wraps pymatgen (structure→pattern) plus cosine similarity to the fixed target. The sim is NumPy and the loop is JAX, so wrap the reward as a host callback / plain black-box scalar — RL never needs it differentiable.
- **Drive it:** `crystalformer/cli/train_ppo.py`, conditioned on the known composition. Knobs: `--beta` (the $\tau$ KL leash to the prior), `--sg_temperature`, `--sg_epsilon`, `--exploration_weight`, `--diversity_weight`.
- **Evaluate:** the fit is your live metric; for the benchmark, structure-match the top candidate to ground truth with pymatgen's `StructureMatcher`.

## Milestones (week-sized)

1. Wire the pymatgen XRD reward; confirm it peaks at the true structure for a simple known case.
2. Recover a handful of known structures from simulated patterns; report recovery rate against a no-prior (random-search) baseline.
3. **Show the prior matters:** sweep the KL strength $\tau$ from no-prior to strong-prior and demonstrate it cures the look-alike-local-minima failure.
4. Stretch: harder chemistries, or experimental opXRD patterns.

## Deliverables

A short study: recovery rate, the $\tau$ ablation, and a comparison against a gradient-descent baseline and/or a random-move Monte Carlo baseline — with a gallery of solved structures next to their patterns. Bounded for a week, with a tail that can become a paper.

## References

- **CrystalFormer** (the prior $p$) — Cao, Luo, Lv, Wang, *Space Group Informed Transformer for Crystalline Materials Generation*, [arXiv:2403.15734](https://arxiv.org/abs/2403.15734); *Science Bulletin* 2025. Code: [deepmodeling/CrystalFormer](https://github.com/deepmodeling/CrystalFormer).
- **CrystalFormer-RL** (the RL loop, shared with #65) — Cao & Wang, *Reinforcement Fine-Tuning for Materials Design*, [arXiv:2504.02367](https://arxiv.org/abs/2504.02367); Phys. Rev. B **113**, 024106 (2026).
- **Why the naive fit is hard** — Segal, Subramanian, Li, Miller, Gómez-Bombarelli, *The loss landscape of powder X-ray diffraction-based structure optimization is too rough for gradient descent*, [arXiv:2512.04036](https://arxiv.org/abs/2512.04036); *Digital Discovery* 2026, DOI 10.1039/D6DD00017G.
- **The classical Monte Carlo ancestor** — Harris, Tremayne, Lightfoot, Bruce, *Crystal Structure Determination from Powder Diffraction Data by Monte Carlo Methods*, J. Am. Chem. Soc. **116**, 3543 (1994).
- **Related ML baseline** — Parackal, Goodall, Faber, Armiento, *Identifying crystal structures beyond known prototypes from x-ray powder diffraction spectra*, Phys. Rev. Materials **8**, 103801 (2024).
- **Tooling** — forward model: pymatgen `XRDCalculator`. Benchmarks: SimXRD-4M ([arXiv:2406.15469](https://arxiv.org/abs/2406.15469)), opXRD ([arXiv:2503.05577](https://arxiv.org/abs/2503.05577)).

Build a fast, low-friction daily challenge system that encourages habit-building without incurring high AI API costs or latency.

To avoid the cost and latency of calling the Gemini AI live every morning for every user:

1. **Dashboard Hook:** A prominent widget at the top of the dashboard: "🎯 Daily Challenge Available! Take 2 minutes to maintain your streak."
2. **The Challenge:** A simple modal or separate page presents the MCQ.
3. **The Reward Loop:** Upon selecting the correct answer:

   - Update `streak.lastActivity` and add to `streak.completedDays`.

1. **Database Schema:** Create a `Challenge` Mongoose model (`question`, `options`, `correctAnswer`, `topic`, `difficulty`).
2. **Backend API:** Create a new route (e.g., `/api/challenges/daily`) that fetches a relevant challenge based on the user's current roadmap progress.

## Overview

Build the core gamification engine that processes application events into XP, levels, predefined achievements, predefined challenges, user progress, recalculation, and reward notifications.

Gamification should be tenant-scoped and powered by predefined application events from `apps/api/src/events/index.ts`.

## User Story

As a learner, I want my progress, consistency, and meaningful engagement to be rewarded automatically, so that I can see clear progress and feel recognized for learning activity.

## Goal

Users should earn XP only from achievement levels and completed challenges.

The system should track lifetime XP, spendable XP, user levels, earned achievements, challenge progress, and recent rewards. It should also support additive-only recalculation from existing activity logs or outbox events.

This task should include the predefined/default achievements and challenges that are seeded per tenant.

## Main User Flow

A user performs an action in the platform, such as logging in, completing a lesson, finishing a quiz, posting in a course chat, receiving a mention, or receiving a like.

From there, the system should:

- Consume the related application event asynchronously.
- Use the existing activity log or outbox event as the source of truth.
- Evaluate matching predefined achievements and challenges.
- Grant newly earned achievement levels.
- Complete eligible challenges.
- Create XP transactions for granted rewards.
- Update lifetime XP and spendable XP.
- Recalculate the user's level from lifetime XP.
- Emit a WebSocket notification when the user earns a reward or levels up.
- Allow the frontend to refetch updated gamification data through REST APIs.

## XP And Levels

The system should distinguish between:

- **Lifetime XP**
  Total XP ever earned. Used for user levels and leaderboards. This should never decrease.

- **Spendable XP**
  XP currently available to spend in the reward shop. This increases when XP is earned and decreases when XP is spent.

User level should be based on total lifetime XP.

XP required to reach level N:

```text
XP required to reach level N = 100 x (N - 1)^2
```

XP required for the next level:

```text
nextLevelXP = 100 x currentLevel^2
xpRemaining = nextLevelXP - totalXP
```

Reward shop spending must never reduce lifetime XP.

## Event Source And Recalculation

Gamification should rely on existing platform records as the source of truth.

The source of truth for recalculation should be either of existing platform records:

- `activityLogs`, when the user action is already represented there.
- `outbox_events`, when the action is represented as a durable domain event.

The gamification module may store derived state and idempotency references, such as earned achievement levels, challenge completions, XP transactions, and the source activity log or outbox event ID that caused a reward.

If a required user action is not currently represented in activity logs or outbox events, the implementation should add or reuse the appropriate existing event/logging mechanism rather than creating a parallel source-of-truth table.

Recalculation should be additive-only. It can grant missing achievements, levels, challenge completions, and XP, but it should not revoke anything or subtract XP.

## Predefined Achievement Rules

Predefined achievements should be seeded per tenant as part of the core setup.

Examples of predefined achievements:

- First login
- Login streak
- Completed lessons
- Completed courses
- Completed quizzes
- High quiz score
- First course chat message
- Received likes on course chat messages
- Being mentioned in course chat

Admins should be able to disable predefined achievements later, but disabling them should not remove historical progress or XP.

## Fairness And Anti-Abuse

The core processor should enforce baseline fairness rules.

Support-mode activity should not create gamification progress.

Duplicate events should not grant duplicate rewards.

Users should not receive XP for liking their own messages.

Admins can earn visible achievements, but they cannot earn hidden achievements.

Students, trainers, and content creators can earn visible and hidden achievements.

## Notifications

When a user earns an achievement, achievement level, challenge completion, or level-up, the backend should emit a WebSocket event to that user.

The frontend should use the event to:

- Show an in-app toast or celebration.
- Invalidate related gamification queries.
- Refetch profile, achievement, challenge, and leaderboard data through REST APIs.

The WebSocket payload does not need to include full leaderboard data.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Application events are consumed asynchronously by the gamification processor.
- Existing activity logs or outbox events are used as the source of truth for processing and recalculation.
- Gamification stores derived progress, rewards, XP transactions, and source references only.
- XP is granted only from achievement levels and completed challenges.
- XP award transactions are stored.
- Lifetime XP and spendable XP are tracked separately.
- User level is calculated from lifetime XP.
- Spendable XP can decrease when spent, but lifetime XP never decreases.
- Predefined achievements are seeded per tenant.
- Disabled predefined rules stop granting new progress without removing historical progress.
- Additive recalculation can grant missing rewards without revoking existing rewards.
- Duplicate events do not grant duplicate XP or rewards.
- Support-mode activity does not create gamification progress.
- Hidden achievement role restrictions are enforced.
- WebSocket reward events are emitted for achievements, challenge completions, and level-ups.
- User progress APIs expose XP, level, earned achievements, challenge progress, and recent rewards.

## Description

Add a **Weekly Challenge Event System** to Bitbrawler — a rotating set of combat modifiers and objectives that give players a reason to return every week. This is the #1 retention mechanic cited by idle game research for 2026.

## Why this fits Bitbrawler

Bitbrawler currently has a solid core loop (create → fight → level → loot → repeat) but lacks **replay incentive** beyond daily reset. Once a player finishes their 5 daily fights and opens their lootbox, there's no reason to come back until the next day. Weekly events fix this by adding **anticipation, variety, and a reason to check in**.

### From web research:
- "Seasonal events every 2-4 weeks can lift D60 retention by 8-15 percentage points" (Game Growth Advisor, 2026)
- "A 14-day event with daily objectives creates habit formation" — the key is **predictable cadence**
- "Small teams should run 2-3 repeatable event patterns, not 10 elaborate ones" (Retention-First Playbook, 2026)

## Design

### Weekly Event Rotation (3 types, cycling):

| Week | Event Type | Modifier | Reward Bonus |
|------|-----------|----------|-------------|
| 1 | **Boss Rush** | All opponents are +2 levels, but drop double XP | Extra lootbox roll |
| 2 | **Glass Arena** | HP halved for both sides, damage doubled | Stat reset token |
| 3 | **Elemental Surge** | Weapon affinity bonuses tripled | Guaranteed uncommon+ item |
| 4 | **Underdog Cup** | Player stats capped at 10, strategy matters | Rare+ lootbox |

### How it works:

1. **Weekly modifier** applies automatically to all arena fights during the event
2. **Event progress bar**: 3 tiers of objectives (win 5/10/15 fights under the modifier)
3. **Reward chest** at each tier — bonus lootbox with better odds
4. **Leaderboard**: Top 10 players by event wins get a Hall of Fame badge

### Implementation scope:

**New files needed:**
- `src/data/events.ts` — Event definitions (modifiers, dates, rewards)
- `src/components/EventBanner.tsx` — UI banner showing active event + progress
- `src/utils/eventUtils.ts` — Event logic (active check, reward calculation)

**Modified files:**
- `src/pages/Arena.tsx` — Apply event modifier to combat calls
- `src/components/CombatView.tsx` — Show event modifier during fight
- `src/config/gameRules.ts` — Add event config constants
- `src/types/` — Add Event types

### Database changes (Supabase):
- New table `events` — Define events (start/end dates, type, rewards)
- New table `player_events` — Track player progress per event

## Impact

| Metric | Expected Improvement |
|--------|---------------------|
| D7 Retention | +5-10 percentage points |
| Avg sessions/week | 7 → 10+ |
| Daily active players | +20-30% during event weeks |
| Player engagement | High — anticipation for weekly reset |

## Effort Estimate

**Effort: 3/5** (moderate)
- Backend: 1 day (Supabase tables + seed data)
- Frontend: 2 days (EventBanner, apply modifiers, progress tracking)
- Testing: 1 day

## Inspiration

- **Egg Inc.** — Contract events with collaborative goals
- **Melvor Idle** — Weekly challenges with modifiers
- **Clicker Heroes** — Clan events and raid bosses
- Research: GameAnalytics "engaging idle games", Retention-First Playbook 2026

Human validation required before implementation.

PoR challenge coverage today is probabilistic, not per-chunk guaranteed. ## Problem

Biome access is gated purely on `usb.biome.<key>` permission nodes (`BiomeCommand`, `BiomeConfig.getAvailableBiomes`). Challenge rewards grant these via `PlayerInfo.addPermissions` → Vault. Two consequences:

- **Without a permissions plugin, biome rewards silently never apply.** Grants park in the player-YAML `pending-permissions` list forever — and that list is re-appended on every skyworld teleport, so it also grows unboundedly (this doubling affects *all* permission rewards on Vault-less servers, not just biomes).
- Biome unlocks are conceptually **island progression** (the biome is an island attribute, challenge progress is island-shared), yet they're materialized as per-player permission state. That mismatch is what forces re-grants on member join, per-member clears on restart, and the associated race conditions.

## Decision

Fold into the 4.0 challenge rework (#119/#128) rather than patching 3.x:

1. **Biome unlocks become island property.** The island earns the unlock; any member with the `canChangeBiome` island permission picks from the island's set. Island create/restart resets unlocks naturally with island state — no per-member clearing policy needed.
2. **Biome rewards become a first-class reward type in the challenge catalog** (e.g. `rewards.biomes: [jungle, ...]`) instead of string-sniffing `usb.biome.*` out of permission rewards at runtime. `reward.permission` stays a pure permission grant.
3. **The legacy importer translates** existing `usb.biome.*` permission-reward entries into biome rewards at challenges.yml import time (#131) — the special-casing happens once, permanently, with operator-visible logging. `usb.biome.*` wildcards expand against the configured biome list (warn on the rest).
4. **The permission gate stays as an OR-fallback** (`hasPermission("usb.biome." + key) || island.hasUnlockedBiome(key)`) for all of 4.x: donor/VIP/op access stays expressible via permissions, and legacy player-level grants keep working without a destructive migration of external permissions data.

## Open sub-decisions for the 4.0 design review

- **Materialized vs derived storage:** store the unlock set on the island, or derive it from the island's completed challenges' biome rewards (+ cache, invalidated on completion/reset)? Derived has no new persistent state, no grant/sync surface, and restart semantics follow challenge reset for free — but couples gating to the challenge subsystem and changes meaning when a challenge's rewards are edited retroactively. Leaning derived, given the catalog rework rebuilds the completion runtime anyway.
- **Default biomes:** replace plugin.yml-default semantics with an operator-controlled `defaultUnlockedBiomes` config (bare biome keys, Registry-validated, warn-and-skip). Decide whether the configured default biome is force-included (guaranteed valid choice) or merely warned about when missing (operators can lock everything; matches the warn-don't-force config philosophy).
- **Grandfathering:** whether to additionally seed island stores from the union of current members' legacy `usb.biome.*` nodes, or rely solely on the OR-fallback aging out.

## Implementation checklist items that an earlier attempt got wrong

(from the adversarial review of branch `independent-biome-unlocking`, commit 65c2dc3b — player-scoped implementation, reviewed and rejected: wrong scope plus ~13 defects)

- `usb.biome.*` wildcard rewards must not collapse to a dead literal `*` entry
- Locale-safe key normalization (`toLowerCase(Locale.ROOT)`), and gate on the Registry-matched biome key, not the raw command argument (`BiomeCommand` already mismatches these for permissions today)
- `getPlayerInfo` can return null (maintenance mode) — no main-thread player-file I/O or NPEs in the GUI filter path
- Don't override existing operator knobs (`options.restart.clearPerms`, `resetChallengesOnCreate`) with hard-coded reset policy
- No destructive removal of `usb.biome.*` nodes from external permissions plugins — leftovers are harmless under the OR gate, and removal is incomplete by construction (offline players, Player-only hook API)
- Update `docs/src/admin/customization.md` (currently: biome access "is controlled by permissions")

Worth keeping from that branch: the dual OR gate, key normalization/dedupe approach, and the config-driven default-unlocked-set concept. The branch itself can be deleted once this issue is the design of record.

## Related

#119 (challenge modernization umbrella), #128 (4.0 gameplay changes), #131 (challenges.yml migration pipeline — importer home), #110 (GUI migration), PR #144 (independent plugin.yml node fixes + NPE guard shipped for 3.x).

## Summary

Bake a small number of deliberate alternate lines into the route data near known
terrain features — e.g. a tighter/rockier shortcut vs. a slower, safer bypass — so
"which line do I take" becomes a real, repeatable route-content decision rather than
just an emergent side effect of open-terrain physics.

## Motivation

Prompted by `docs/route-challenge-design.md`, which maps out the decisions a player
currently makes while riding a route (line choice through a corner, how much speed to
carry, when to spend boost, jump commitment) and finds that all of them are
*emergent* from the physics/scoring model rather than *authored* into the route
itself. Every other item in that doc's decisions table is already backed by code
(`BikeController.js`'s friction circle, `ScoreTracker.js`'s flow/trick scoring); this
is the one gap that needs actual route-content changes, not just a code change.

`public/data/routes/cutgate.json` today is a flat `points` array (easting/northing
control points reprojected by `routePointToWorld`) with no concept of a branch —
`src/routes/RouteOverlay.js` turns it straight into a single `CatmullRomCurve3`.

## Proposed scope

- Extend the baked route JSON schema with an optional way to mark a short alternate
  segment near a subset of existing points — e.g. a small side-array of alternate
  points spanning the same terrain, tagged with a difficulty/risk label.
- `RouteOverlay.js` renders both the main line and alternate segment(s) (distinct
  styling, e.g. a slightly different `ROUTE_STYLE` tint) rather than gameplay logic
  picking one — the player should be able to *see* the fork exists.
- Each alternate line's scoring profile differs (tighter/rockier could pay more via
  `TERRAIN_BONUS`-style factors already in `ScoreTracker.js`, or carry more crash
  risk from tighter geometry) rather than needing a new scoring mechanism.
- No forced choice or invisible walls — matches the existing open-terrain sandbox
  feel; a player can still ignore both authored lines entirely.

## Out of scope

- A generic branching-route editor/tooling — a couple of hand-authored forks on the
  existing Cut Gate route (or whichever route ships next via #52/#134) is the ask,
  not a full authoring tool.
- Any change to how many *routes* exist (#52/#134) — this is about within-route
  line choice, not additional real-world descents.

## Open questions

- Does this land against the current Cut Gate route, or wait for a second real route
  (#52/#134) so the authoring effort isn't spent twice on data that might get
  restructured by the pipeline generalisation in #47?
- Best data shape for an "alternate segment" that stays simple to author by hand
  (matching how `tools/terrain/` already works) rather than needing a graph structure.

## References

- `docs/route-challenge-design.md` — decisions/skills analysis this issue serves.

## Scheduling & lazy processing

The design's principle is to **avoid periodic/scheduled on-chain work** (the chain is "a credible threat, not the hot path" — explicitly contrasted with Filecoin's per-sector periodic proofs). So almost everything is intentionally pull / event / off-chain. The one thing the design *does* schedule is challenge-timeout slashing, processed at the deadline block.

The **Implement?** column is validated against the canonical design (#170).

| Concern | Deadline source | Current handling | Implement? |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Challenge timeout → slash** | `Challenges[deadline_block]`, `deadline = now + ChallengeTimeout` | `on_finalize(n)` slashes every challenge maturing at block `n` | 🟡 **Keep scheduled (by design); harden only.** Design intends deadline-block processing and considers the batch bounded-by-weight (all challenges at `n` were created at the single block `n − ChallengeTimeout`). Not a design gap. Defensive hardening: make the bound explicit (`BoundedVec`) and consider moving the slashing off `on_finalize` (critical path) to `on_idle`/`on_poll` |
| **Agreement expiry** (`expires_at`) | per-agreement field | Pull: `end_agreement` (owner) / `claim_expired_agreement` (provider) | ⚠️ **Optional / low.** Pull is by design; only consider cleanup for the residual where neither party acts |
| **Missed checkpoint → slash** | checkpoint window + grace | Pull + incentivized: `report_missed_checkpoint` (reporter gets 10%) | ❌ **No (works as designed).** 10% reporter reward is canonical; at most document it |
| **Agreement request expiry** (`RequestTimeout`) | config (6h) | None — only a `// TODO` in `provider-node/src/api.rs:815` | 🟡 **Decision first.** Design↔code divergence: design (#170) keeps on-chain requests with `expires_at`; code (#105) moved negotiation off-chain. Reconcile, then implement lazy expiry only if requests stay on-chain |
| **Deregistration** | `deregister_at = now + DeregisterAnnouncementPeriod` | Pull: announce → wait → `complete_deregister` | ❌ **No.** Two-phase pull is intended |

## Goal

Close the loop so the CUA agent improves from its own traces — **execute → observe → reward → curate → improve → evaluate → promote → repeat** — safely and on a schedule. We already have the execution plane (Mantis) and the data plane (Augur). This epic builds the missing connective tissue.

## Where each piece lives (repo placement)

The existing two-repo split maps onto the architecture; the trainer becomes a third repo.

| Plane | Repo | Owns |
|---|---|---|
| **Data** | `augur-sdk` (existing) | trace capture ✅, `modelio`/logprobs/`group_id`/`task_spec` ✅, `set_score` ✅, **dataset curation + reward schema + eval-candidate selection** (extend) |
| **Agent + fast loop + controller** | `mantis` (here) | execution ✅, reward verifiers, champion/challenger gate, flywheel controller, non-param improvement (`recipes`/`curriculum`/`hint_memory`/`learning`) |
| **Slow loop (weights)** | **new repo `mantis-trainer`** (later) | GRPO/SFT/DPO trainer, checkpoint/model registry. Heavy torch/vLLM + GPU footprint — kept out of the SDK and the runtime. Consumes Augur datasets, emits weights Mantis/Baseten deploy. |

**Rule:** data plane → Augur · agent + fast loop + controller + gate → Mantis · weight training → new repo. Augur never imports execution/training.

## Two loops (drives sequencing)

- **Fast loop (non-parametric, hours, no GPU):** traces → curate → update memory/recipes/hints/curriculum/exemplars → better behavior without touching weights. **~80% already in Mantis** (`learning/`, `rewards/`, `curriculum/`, `recipes/plan_evolution_store`, `hint_memory`, `learning/substrates`). Build this FIRST.
- **Slow loop (parametric, days, GPU):** traces → modelio dataset → GRPO/SFT → new Holo3 weights → gate → deploy. Data pipeline exists; trainer does not. Build AFTER the reward + gate are proven.

## Missing load-bearing components (priority order)

### 1. Reward / verification on real traffic  — the universal bottleneck
Sim envs have oracles (ground truth); real sites don't. `set_score` is a hook with no scorer. Need outcome verifiers: programmatic post-conditions per task type, LLM-judge ensembles (reuse our adversarial-verify pattern), and **implicit/human signals — the pause/resume hand-off is already a labeling channel**. Gates how much real data becomes trainable. (Mantis: verifiers · Augur: reward storage/schema.)

### 2. Champion/challenger promotion gate over a frozen benchmark
Lets us close ANY loop safely. Today nothing answers "does candidate beat the deployed champion by X% at $Y/run, significantly?" Seeds exist: sim envs = benchmark, `shadow_router.py` = shadow traffic, `learning/eval.py` = scoring. Missing: the gate — frozen eval set + statistical comparison + auto-promote/rollback. (Mantis.)

### 3. Flywheel controller
`learning/orchestrator.py` + `learning/allocator.py` are the skeleton but hand-cranked. Need the standing loop: schedule exploration (target `failure_clusters`, not just replay wins) → collect → curate → apply improvement → run gate → promote → repeat, with budget governance. (Mantis.)

### 4. Weight-update trainer (slow loop)
Only genuinely new infra. Data is already RL-shaped (`modelio` OpenAI shape, `group_id` GRPO siblings, logprobs, `task_spec`) with no consumer. (New repo.)

### Cross-cutting
- **Credit assignment / per-step reward** — per-step `set_score` hook exists, scorer doesn't (coarse sparks observed in #892). Process reward model or step verifiers.
- **Curation policy** — dedup via `trajectory_fingerprint` ✅; need positive/negative selection, quality filtering, balancing on top of Augur `build_dataset`.
- **Autonomy guardrails** — cost caps ✅, human gates (pause/resume) ✅; need rollback + blast-radius limits for real-site actions.

## Phased plan

- **Phase 0 — minimal closed loop on ONE sim env (ground-truth reward).** explore → score (oracle) → curate failures → update hints/recipes → gate against frozen tasks → auto-promote. Proves loop mechanics with trustworthy reward. **First buildable milestone.**
- **Phase 1 — fast loop on real traffic.** Generalize reward (verifiers + implicit signals) beyond sim; harden the gate; stand up the controller on a schedule with budget governance.
- **Phase 2 — slow loop.** New `mantis-trainer` repo; GRPO/SFT over Augur datasets; champion/challenger over weights through the same gate.

## Acceptance (Phase 0)
- [ ] One sim env runs a fully automated explore→score→curate→update→gate→promote cycle with no human step.
- [ ] The gate blocks a deliberately-regressed candidate and promotes a genuinely-better one.
- [ ] Reward comes from the env oracle (no hand-labeling); improvement is non-parametric (recipes/hints).
- [ ] A run-list / report shows champion vs challenger deltas at fixed cost budget.

## Sub-issues to file
- [ ] Mantis: reward verifier interface + per-task post-conditions (#1)
- [ ] Mantis: champion/challenger promotion gate over frozen benchmark (#2)
- [ ] Mantis: flywheel controller / closed-loop runner (#3)
- [ ] `augur-sdk`: dataset curation policy + reward-schema extensions (data plane)
- [ ] New repo `mantis-trainer`: GRPO/SFT trainer scaffold (#4, Phase 2)

## Summary

If a node's operational wallet is a smart contract, it may be able to grind `RandomSampling.createChallenge()` by previewing the challenge in the same transaction and reverting when the draw is unfavorable.

## Why This Matters

EOA operational wallet:

```text
call createChallenge()
accept whatever challenge is produced
```

Contract operational wallet:

```text
call preview / simulate picker inside tx
if challenge is bad: revert
if challenge is good: proceed to createChallenge()
```

This can bias proof/reward sampling. It is not direct token theft, but it weakens the randomness/proof-of-storage incentive model.

## Code References

- `packages/evm-module/contracts/RandomSampling.sol`
  - `createChallenge()` calls `_generateChallenge(msg.sender)` and stores the challenge afterward.
  - `_deriveChallengeSeed` uses block state plus `originalSender`.
  - `previewChallengeForSeed` exposes the same picker for arbitrary seeds.
- `packages/evm-module/contracts/Profile.sol` / `Identity.sol`
  - operational wallets are added by address; there is no apparent EOA-only restriction.

## Expected Behavior

A node should not be able to reject unfavorable challenge draws without committing to them.

## Actual Behavior

A contract operational wallet can potentially make challenge creation conditional on the sampled result by reverting before storage is updated.

## Validation Needed

- Add a minimal test contract operational wallet:
  1. Register it as an operational wallet.
  2. In one call, derive/preview the challenge outcome.
  3. Revert on unfavorable outcome.
  4. Show that no challenge is stored on revert and retries can continue.

## Suggested Fix Direction

Long-term: commit-reveal or VRF-style randomness.

Short-term options:

- disallow contract operational wallets for challenge creation, or
- force challenge commitment before any caller-controlled callback/branching is possible.

## Context

Optional post-release enhancement to **Roguelite Challenge Mode (#79)** — blocked by #79. Inspired by Darkest Dungeon's torch/light meter: lower light means more danger but better loot, up to Pitch Black runs. LC has no continuous difficulty dial — challenge is all-or-nothing. This adds a day-start "facility power" slider: turn it down for a harder, more rewarding day.

This is a redesign of an earlier pitch whose two proposed levers turned out not to work as assumed (see Research notes); the danger and reward mechanisms below are the corrected versions.

## Player value

Challenge-runners and streamers who want a self-set difficulty knob that actually pays out, instead of binary challenge modes. Regular players can run it mild for slightly spicier days. Because rewards scale smoothly, it survives the retry meta — rewinding a failed low-power day just re-attempts the same bet.

## Design

Lower facility power:
- **Danger:** a Postfix on `CreatureModel.GetWorkSuccessProb` reduces/widens work success; failed work decays the qliphoth counter faster (`Add`/`Sub`/`SetQliphothCounter`); meltdown pressure rises via `CreatureOverloadManager.AddOverloadGague()`.
- **Reward (independent of any other mod):** a stat-growth multiplier on the `primaryStatExp` path, plus an end-of-day LOB bounty scaled by the dial. **If** the Department Upgrade System enhancement is installed, the dial *also* multiplies department-crest yield — a soft synergy, not a hard dependency.

Config: dial level + curve presets (locked at day start by default; live-adjust optional), per-lever toggles.

## Research notes (decompiled source, verified)

- `CreatureModel.GetWorkSuccessProb(AgentModel, SkillTypeInfo)` is public; the roll is `Random.value < workSuccessProb` in `UseSkill.ProcessWorkTick`.
- `CreatureModel.Add`/`Sub`/`SetQliphothCounter` are public.
- `CreatureOverloadManager.AddOverloadGague()` is public and drives the meltdown/overload gauge (note the in-game misspelling "Gague").
- Stat growth: exp is granted via `agent.primaryStatExp` (`.hp`/`.mental`/`.work`/`.battle`) in `UseSkill.CloseWork`; `AgentModel.CalculateStatLevel` is static.
- **Rejected levers (why this is a redesign):** `EnergyModel.AddEnergy` clamps at the day quota (`GetEnergyNeed(day)`), so multiplying energy yields no surplus — energy is NOT used as the reward. `EmergencyController` score only drives BGM/alarm UI, not difficulty — NOT used for the danger lever.

## Open questions

- Exact danger curve, and whether the dial is per-day or per-run.
- Crest-yield multiplier magnitude (only relevant alongside the Department Upgrade System).
- Gift-chance bonus stays OFF by default to avoid stepping on Bad Luck Protection.

## Scope

Medium. Logic separates cleanly into testable extension methods. Must stay a continuous opt-in dial (never a binary mode) and stay distinct from #139 (forced worst-case) and #79 (the mode itself) — note both in the README.

- [ ] Encode tier gating in each rank's `unlock` block per the draft (island-level thresholds, prerequisite challenges, the n-of-9 completion gates, and the tier convergence), and set rank `display` / `lockedDisplayItem` and per-challenge text.
- [ ] Bundle the result *as* `schemaVersion: 1` so admins see the new schema directly; reserve the first-boot `LegacyChallengeCatalogImporter` for upgrading existing servers' legacy files.
