# Proposition: Progressive Daily Login Reward System — retention via exponential streak

**Type: Proposition majeure** (validation humaine)

---

## Analyse

### Problème identifié

Bitbrawler n'a actuellement **aucun système de récompense de connexion quotidienne**. Les joueurs:
1. Reviennent uniquement pour leurs 5 combats PvP quotidiens
2. N'ont pas d'incitation supplémentaire à se connecter
3. Ne sont pas récompensés pour leur fidélité
4. N'ont pas de "FOMO" (Fear Of Missing Out) qui les pousse à revenir

### Opportunité

La recherche web (2026) montre clairement l'importance des daily login rewards:

1. **Exponential reward curves**: "Flat daily login bonuses are dead. The best-performing retention tactics use exponential reward curves that create increasing value over consecutive days. Missing a day should feel costly, but not punishing enough to cause permanent churn." — Game Growth Advisor, 2026

2. **Progressive rewards**: "Structure your reward calendar so that the Day 7 reward is significantly more valuable than Day 1-6 combined. This creates a psychological commitment that drives D7 retention."

3. **Idle game best practices**: "Daily rewards, login bonuses, and simple quest systems can encourage regular play sessions." — DesignTheGame.com

4. **Prestige-compatible**: Les systèmes de daily login sont complémentaires avec les systèmes de prestige (#274, #285, #309, #321) — les joueurs qui prestigient gardent leur streak, ce qui adoucit la perte de progression.

### Différence avec les propositions existantes

| Issue | Focus | Différence |
|-------|-------|------------|
| #164, #275, #302, #286 | **Daily Challenges** (tâches à accomplir) | Complexe, nécessite UI/UX, design de quêtes |
| **Cette proposition** | **Daily Login Reward** (connexion seule) | Simple, juste "connecte-toi et reçois" |

Ces deux systèmes sont complémentaires — le login reward est un prérequis plus simple.

---

## Solution proposée

### Système: "Daily Streak Rewards"

**1. Structure de récompense exponentielle**

| Jour | Récompense | Notes |
|-----|-----------|-------|
| J1 | 50 XP | Rampe douce |
| J2 | 75 XP | |
| J3 | 100 XP + 1 Common Lootbox | |
| J4 | 125 XP | |
| J5 | 150 XP + 1 Uncommon Lootbox | |
| J6 | 175 XP | |
| **J7** | **250 XP + 1 Rare Lootbox + 2 bonus stat points** | Pic hebdomadaire |
| J8-J13 | Reprend la progression (200-300 XP/jour) | |
| **J14** | **400 XP + 1 Epic Lootbox + 3 bonus stat points** | Pic bi-hebdomadaire |
| J15-J29 | Continue (300-400 XP/jour) | |
| **J30** | **1000 XP + 1 Legendary Lootbox + 5 bonus stat points + exclusive cosmetic** | Méga-récompense mensuelle |

**2. Règle de streak**
- Se connecter chaque jour = streak continue
- **Un "joker" gratuit par semaine**: si le joueur manque un jour, son streak est sauvegardé (consomme le joker)
- Si plus de 1 jour manqué: streak reset à J1 (avec un message encouraging)
- Les bonus stat points sont temporaires (durent 24h) ou permanents (à débattre)

**3. Intégration UI minimale**
- Une pop-up au premier chargement de la journée: "Day X streak! Claim your reward!"
- Un petit indicateur dans le header: "🔥 Day 3"
- Pas de nouvelle page ou écran complexe

**4. Complément avec les systèmes existants**
- Le streak de lootbox (#329, système STREAK_TIERS déjà existant dans lootboxUtils.ts) peut être fusionné ou rendu compatible
- Le daily reset (déjà implémenté) gère la logique de changement de jour
- Pas de conflit avec les daily challenges (futur)

---

## Pourquoi c'est adapté à Bitbrawler

1. **Mobile-first**: Une pop-up au login = parfait pour mobile
2. **Pixel art**: Une simple animation pixel de coffre qui s'ouvre = peu de ressources
3. **Idle-friendly**: Pas besoin de jouer, juste se connecter
4. **Retention prouvée**: Les benchmarks 2026 montrent +15-30% D7 retention
5. **Faible effort**: Pas de nouveau mode de jeu, pas de nouvelle mécanique complexe
6. **Prérequis pour d'autres features**: Un daily login system est le socle pour les daily challenges, events, etc.

## Impact

🟠 **Impact estimé: Medium-High**

| Métrique | Impact estimé |
|----------|--------------|
| D7 Retention | +15-25% |
| D30 Retention | +8-12% |
| Sessions/jour | +0.5-1 session |
| Temps par session | Stable (juste login) |
| Rétention après prestige | Améliorée (streak preserve adoucit le reset) |

## Effort

**Effort: 2/5** (implémentation simple)

| Composant | Effort | Détails |
|-----------|--------|---------|
| DB schema | 0.5 | 1 colonne: `last_login_date`, `login_streak` sur la table characters |
| Streak logic | 0.5 | Fonction pure: calculer le streak, date du dernier login, date du joker |
| Reward config | 0.5 | Constantes dans gameRules.ts: récompenses par jour |
| UI popup | 1 | Composant React: pop-up de claim + indicateur header |
| Tests | 0.5 | Tests unitaires pour la logique de streak + récompenses |
| QA bot update | 0.5 | Le bot doit tester le claim de daily reward |

## Inspiré de

- **Game Growth Advisor** (2026) — "exponential reward curves" pour D7 retention
- **DesignTheGame.com** — idle game design patterns: daily rewards as core retention
- **Idle Miner Tycoon** — streak system with exponential value increase
- **Egg, Inc.** — daily gifts with escalating rewards (common → legendary)
- **Cookie Clicker** — golden cookies + daily login bonuses
- **Monopoly GO!** — extremely successful daily login + events system ($2B+ revenue)
title: Proposition: Progressive Daily Login Reward System — exponential streak for retention

## Summary

Replace per-kid weekly goal bonuses with a family-wide **Weekly Dungeon** — a cooperative challenge where all kids contribute damage by completing quests. When the dungeon is cleared, every kid earns a flat coin+XP reward.

## Design

### How it works
- Parent manually creates a dungeon run for the week (or skips — fully optional)
- The dungeon has a HP total (e.g. 300 coins of damage needed)
- Every approved quest deals damage = `coins_awarded` to the dungeon pool
- When `current_damage >= hp`, the dungeon is **cleared**: every kid in the family instantly earns `reward_coins` and `reward_xp`
- Cleared dungeons go into a history log (parent can see past victories)

### Why family-wide, not per-kid
Cooperative mechanics build positive sibling dynamics — kids root for each other instead of competing. One kid doing extra quests helps everyone.

### HP calibration example
- 3 kids × avg 15 coins/quest × 7 days × ~50% completion = ~158 coins/week
- A 200 HP dungeon is achievable; a 400 HP dungeon is a stretch goal

### Rewards
- Parent sets flat `reward_coins` per kid (e.g. 50) and `reward_xp` per kid (e.g. 100)
- Displayed as the dungeon's "loot" before it's cleared

## Schema

```sql
create table dungeon_runs (
  id uuid primary key default gen_random_uuid(),
  family_id uuid not null references families(id) on delete cascade,
  title text not null default 'Weekly Dungeon',
  icon text not null default '🏰',
  hp integer not null,
  current_damage integer not null default 0,
  reward_coins integer not null default 50,
  reward_xp integer not null default 100,
  week_start date not null,
  status text not null default 'active',  -- 'active' | 'cleared'
  cleared_at timestamptz,
  created_at timestamptz default now(),
  unique(family_id, week_start)
);
```

## Implementation phases

1. Schema migration + RLS
2. Dungeon damage in quest approval flow (`use-parent-actions.ts`)
3. Parent UI: create dungeon run (title, icon, HP, reward) + progress panel
4. Display wall: dungeon HP bar visible to all kids
5. Kid view: show active dungeon progress + "your damage dealt" contribution
6. Cleared dungeon celebration animation + history log

## Notes
- Remove per-kid `weekly_goal_paid_week` payout from `approve()` — replaced by this system
- Optional: families that don't create a dungeon run see nothing extra
- Plan gate: Family plan and above
title: Weekly Dungeon: family-wide cooperative challenge with flat coin+XP reward

**Goal:**
Reward Pokémon with small amounts of EXP for helping with overworld field actions, inspired by Legends-style move EXP. Toggle in settings.

**Design:**

* Certain successful field actions grant a small amount of EXP.
* EXP should only be awarded when the action actually changes the overworld or progresses a puzzle.
* EXP should go to the lead Pokémon, follower Pokémon, or the Pokémon associated with the field action if one exists.
* If following Pokémon are enabled, flavor text can imply the follower helped.
* EXP should respect level caps if Challenge Mode level caps are enabled.
* Fainted Pokémon should not receive field action EXP.
* Field action EXP should not be infinitely farmable.

**Suggested EXP values:**

* Cut tree removed: 25 EXP
* Rock Smash rock broken: 25–50 EXP
* Strength puzzle action: 50–100 EXP once per puzzle or once per room
* Flash used successfully in a dark area: 25 EXP once per area
* Surf/Dive/Waterfall: optional, likely no repeatable EXP or only once per route/area

**Recommended first version:**

* Cut: 25 EXP when a tree is removed
* Rock Smash: 25 EXP when a rock is broken
* Strength: 75 EXP once per puzzle/room after a meaningful boulder movement or puzzle completion

**Postgame obstacle cleanup:**

* No repeatable EXP.
* Optional one-time area bonus only if desired.
* Cleanup should mainly be convenience, not a grind source.

**Rules:**

* Do not award EXP for failed actions.
* Do not award EXP if the obstacle has already been cleared.
* Do not award EXP repeatedly from the same Strength boulder.
* Do not award EXP from postgame auto-cleanup unless explicitly designed.
* Do not award EXP if the selected recipient is fainted.
* Respect level cap settings.
* Trigger level-up/evolution handling safely if field EXP causes a level-up.

**Possible messages:**

* “{POKEMON} gained a little EXP for helping out!”
* “{POKEMON} gained 25 EXP!”
* “{POKEMON} looked proud of its hard work.”
* If follower reactions are enabled: “{FOLLOWER} helped clear the way!”

## Summary

Tracking issue for `docs/route-challenge-design.md`, a design doc analysing what
makes following the route itself interesting and challenging: what decisions a
player gets to make on a run, what skills those decisions demand, and how the
existing scoring model should (and currently doesn't) reward getting them right.

## Why this doc, now

`src/routes/RouteOverlay.js` is explicitly decorative today (`CLAUDE.md`: "no
gameplay coupling") — `main.js` only reads the route's first point to place the
spawn. Meanwhile `src/bike/BikeController.js` already has real friction-circle
physics and a stamina/boost resource, and `src/scoring/ScoreTracker.js` already has
THPS-style flow/trick/combo scoring — none of it cares whether the player is
anywhere near the route. The highest-scoring play today is arguably to leave the
route for the steepest, rockiest terrain available. This is a companion lens to
#161 (MDA framework) and #164 (competitive positioning) — same "connect the backlog
to a throughline" approach, applied specifically to the route-following question
issue #137 already asked ("reduce score away from trail?").

## What the doc found

A decisions/skills table mapping each player decision (line choice through a corner,
how much speed to carry, when to spend boost, jump commitment, keeping a combo alive)
to the code that already supports it — all of it emergent from physics/scoring, none
of it tied to the route specifically. The one true gap: nothing rewards or requires
staying near the authored route line.

## Mapping to the backlog

- **#137** ("reduce score away from trail?") — updated with the concrete design this
  doc proposes: a route-adherence multiplier in `ScoreTracker.js`, same shape as its
  existing `TERRAIN_BONUS`.
- **#64** (sessions/scoring/leaderboards) — checkpoint/split-time gates are a slice
  of this, not a separate issue.
- **#65** (ghost replay / run comparison) — already covers the
  mastery-through-repetition angle.
- **#129** (charge-and-release jump) — sharpens the "jump commitment" decision.
- **#62** (gear mechanic) — a second lever on speed-management decisions.
- **#170** (new) — risk/reward alternate route lines, the one gap needing route
  *content* rather than code, filed since nothing existing covered it.

## Recommended sequencing

Land the #137 route-adherence multiplier first (small, self-contained, directly
answers an existing open question), then #64's checkpoint/split-time slice
(shares session-state groundwork with #65), then treat #170 (alternate lines) as
route-content work once a second real route (#52/#134) is also on the table.

## Explicitly out of scope

- Hard corridor enforcement (invisible walls / forced slowdown off-route) —
  contradicts the existing open-terrain sandbox feel; the multiplier approach gets
  the same incentive without removing player freedom.
- Trick-depth expansion for its own sake — already an open question against
  `ScoreTracker.js`'s combo model in #161, not what this doc is about.

## Acceptance criteria

- `docs/route-challenge-design.md` lands (this PR/commit).
- #137 is updated with the concrete design rather than left as an open question.
- New gap identified (#170) is filed and cross-linked here rather than duplicating
  existing backlog.
- This issue stays open as the map between the doc and the backlog until the
  recommended sequencing above is substantially acted on, then can close.

### What is your suggestion?

Feature Proposal: Community Weekly/Daily Challenges Based on SCUM.db Statistics

I would like to suggest a built-in Weekly/Daily Community Challenge system for ggCON.

The basic idea is that server owners can define community-wide goals based on existing statistics from the SCUM database. Players or squads contribute naturally while playing, and when the target is reached, the server owner can unlock a temporary reward manually, for example boosted skill gain, shop rewards, base building expansion kits, or special server events.

Example challenges:

* Weekly: Kill 5,000 puppets
* Daily: Kill 250 animals
* Weekly: Loot 10,000 containers
* Daily: Travel 100,000 meters by foot
* Weekly: Fire 50,000 shots

The required data already exists in the `survival_stats` table of `SCUM.db`.

Relevant table:

```sql
CREATE TABLE survival_stats
(
    user_profile_id INTEGER NOT NULL,
    animals_killed INTEGER DEFAULT 0,
    kills INTEGER DEFAULT 0,
    deaths INTEGER DEFAULT 0,
    locks_picked INTEGER DEFAULT 0,
    puppets_killed INTEGER DEFAULT 0,
    guns_crafted INTEGER DEFAULT 0,
    bullets_crafted INTEGER DEFAULT 0,
    arrows_crafted INTEGER DEFAULT 0,
    clothing_crafted INTEGER DEFAULT 0,
    melee_kills INTEGER DEFAULT 0,
    archery_kills INTEGER DEFAULT 0,
    containers_looted INTEGER DEFAULT 0,
    items_put_into_containers INTEGER DEFAULT 0,
    animals_skinned INTEGER DEFAULT 0,
    distance_travelled_by_foot REAL DEFAULT 0.0,
    wounds_patched INTEGER DEFAULT 0,
    items_picked_up INTEGER DEFAULT 0,
    shots_fired INTEGER DEFAULT 0,
    shots_hit INTEGER DEFAULT 0,
    headshots INTEGER DEFAULT 0,
    melee_weapon_swings INTEGER DEFAULT 0,
    melee_weapon_hits INTEGER DEFAULT 0,
    melee_weapons_crafted INTEGER DEFAULT 0,
    drone_kills INTEGER DEFAULT 0,
    sentry_kills INTEGER DEFAULT 0,
    prisoner_kills INTEGER DEFAULT 0,
    puppets_knocked_out INTEGER DEFAULT 0,
    distance_travelled_in_vehicle REAL DEFAULT 0.0,
    mushrooms_eaten INTEGER DEFAULT 0,
    distance_travelled_swimming REAL DEFAULT 0.0,
    crows_killed INTEGER DEFAULT 0,
    seagulls_killed INTEGER DEFAULT 0,
    horses_killed INTEGER DEFAULT 0,
    boars_killed INTEGER DEFAULT 0,
    bears_killed INTEGER DEFAULT 0,
    goats_killed INTEGER DEFAULT 0,
    deers_killed INTEGER DEFAULT 0,
    chickens_killed INTEGER DEFAULT 0,
    rabbits_killed INTEGER DEFAULT 0,
    donkeys_killed INTEGER DEFAULT 0,
    alcohol_drank INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
    foliage_cut INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
    distance_travel_by_boat REAL NOT NULL DEFAULT 0.0,
    distance_sailed REAL NOT NULL DEFAULT 0.0,
    wolves_killed INTEGER DEFAULT 0,
    firearm_kills INTEGER DEFAULT 0,
    bare_handed_kills INTEGER DEFAULT 0,

    PRIMARY KEY(user_profile_id),
    FOREIGN KEY(user_profile_id) REFERENCES user_profile(id) ON DELETE CASCADE
);
```

A challenge system could work like this:

1. At challenge start, ggCON stores the current baseline value of the selected statistic.
2. During the challenge, ggCON checks the current value periodically.
3. Progress is calculated as:

```text
current_stat_sum - baseline_stat_sum
```

4. The result can be posted to Discord and optionally announced ingame.
5. When the target is reached, the challenge is marked as completed.
6. The server owner can manually activate the reward for a defined duration.

Example configuration:

```json
{
  "enabled": true,
  "id": "weekly-puppets",
  "type": "Weekly",
  "title": "Zombie Hunt",
  "description": "Kill 5,000 puppets as a community.",
  "statColumn": "puppets_killed",
  "target": 5000,
  "durationHours": 168,
  "minimumParticipationPercent": 2.0,
  "rewardText": "Each participating squad receives one Level 1 Basebuilding Expansion Kit.",
  "completedText": "Challenge completed! Contact an admin to claim your reward."
}
```

Squad contribution could also be calculated by joining `survival_stats`, `squad_member`, and `squad`:

```sql
SELECT
    squad.name,
    SUM(survival_stats.puppets_killed) AS value
FROM survival_stats
JOIN squad_member ON squad_member.user_profile_id = survival_stats.user_profile_id
JOIN squad ON squad.id = squad_member.squad_id
GROUP BY squad.id, squad.name;
```

To avoid rewarding squads that only contributed a very small amount, a minimum participation threshold could be used, for example 2% of the target value, rounded down.

Example:

```text
Target: 5,000 puppet kills
Minimum squad contribution: 2% = 100 kills
```

Only squads that reach this minimum contribution would be shown as successful participants.

This would be a very useful feature for PvE and community servers because it creates long-term motivation without requiring custom scripts or manual database analysis.

  ```typescript
  const fetcher = useCallback(async () => {
    if (!challengeId) return null;
    const { data } = await supabase
      .from('challenges')
      .select('*')
      .eq('id', challengeId)
      .single();
    return data;
  }, [challengeId]);
  ```

  ```
  │ ← Back                          │

  │ [Type Icon - large]             │
  │                                 │
  │ Challenge Title                 │

  │ ┌─────────────────────────────┐ │
  │ │    Accept Challenge ✓       │ │
  │ └─────────────────────────────┘ │
  ```

  - **Duration**: Compute from cadence or start/end dates (e.g., "7 days", "30 days")
  - **Points**: `{points_reward} pts`

  ```typescript

  const handleAccept = async () => {
    setAccepting(true);
    const result = await pickChallenge(user!.id, challengeId!);
    setAccepting(false);

    if (result.success) {
  ```

  - Limit reached: show "You've reached your {cadence} limit" message


**Summary:** Biome painting works on `feature/immutable-challenge-catalog`, but the biome-reward feature is unfinished: nether biomes can be painted in the overworld (no dimension guard), the catalog still grants biomes through legacy `usb.biome.*` permission rewards instead of the new island-scoped `BiomeReward`, and the permission-independence work sits on an unmerged branch.

## Why this blocks 4.0
The 4.0 readiness survey flags biome unlocking as a first-class challenge reward (#145), and the plumbing is mostly in place — `IslandBiomeUnlocks`, the `BiomeReward` reward action, and a YAML `type: biome` parser all exist. But the shipping catalog never actually uses any of it: every biome grant in `challenges.yml` is still a raw `permission: usb.biome.<key>` reward, so islands cannot earn biomes without an external permissions plugin, and the new island-derived unlock path is dead. On top of that, `/is biome` will happily paint a nether biome into the overworld skyblock world because there is no dimension restriction anywhere in the paint path. These are correctness/feature gaps that make biome rewards effectively non-functional for a stock 4.0 install.

## Current state
- Painting itself works: `SetBiomeTask.execute()` calls `world.setBiome(x, y, z, biome)` (`uSkyBlock-Core/src/main/java/us/talabrek/ultimateskyblock/island/task/SetBiomeTask.java:82`), and `BiomeCommand` dispatches it against `player.getWorld()` (`uSkyBlock-Core/src/main/java/us/talabrek/ultimateskyblock/command/island/BiomeCommand.java:136`).
- The biome catalog defines 18 biomes, each resolved against the live registry via `Registry.BIOME.match(biomeKey)`, warning on unknown keys (`uSkyBlock-Core/src/main/java/us/talabrek/ultimateskyblock/biome/BiomeConfig.java:70`, warning at line 72). The list includes nether/end biomes — `nether_wastes` and `the_end` (`uSkyBlock-Core/src/main/resources/biomes.yml`).
- No dimension restriction exists. A `git grep -niE "Environment|NETHER|getEnvironment"` across `.../biome/` and `SetBiomeTask.java` returns nothing, and `BiomeCommand` paints into `player.getWorld()` with no `World.Environment.NETHER` guard — so a nether biome can be applied in the overworld.
- The island-unlock infrastructure is present but unused by the catalog: the `BiomeReward(List<String> biomes)` reward action (`uSkyBlock-Core/src/main/java/us/talabrek/ultimateskyblock/challenge/catalog/ChallengeRewards.java:38`), the `type: biome` YAML parser branch (`uSkyBlock-Core/src/main/java/us/talabrek/ultimateskyblock/challenge/catalog/yaml/ChallengeCatalogYamlParser.java:271`), and `IslandBiomeUnlocks` which derives unlocks from completed challenges and gates `/is biome` via `canUseBiome` (`uSkyBlock-Core/src/main/java/us/talabrek/ultimateskyblock/challenge/IslandBiomeUnlocks.java:65`, called at `BiomeCommand.java:94`).
- But the shipped catalog still grants biomes the legacy way: `challenges.yml` contains only `permission: usb.biome.<key>` rewards (lines 786, 831, 968, 1068, 1121), covering just three distinct biomes — `deep_ocean`, `flower_forest`, `swamp`. There are zero `type: biome` rewards authored anywhere in `src/main/resources`.
- `canUseBiome` deliberately keeps the personal `usb.biome.<key>` permission as an OR-fallback alongside the island-earned unlock (`IslandBiomeUnlocks.java:65-67`), so permission-based grants are meant to coexist, not be the primary path.
- The permission-independence work is unmerged. Branch `independent-biome-unlocking` is a single commit ahead of the catalog branch — `65c2dc3b` ("make biome unlocking independent of an installed permissions plugin. Migrate legacy, permission-based unlocks.") — which adds `general_defaultUnlockedBiomes` to `Settings.java` (with a `Registry.BIOME.match` validation pass and a `usb.biome.` prefix strip) plus config/plugin.yml and `PlayerInfo` migration logic.

## Scope
- [ ] Add a dimension restriction so nether/end biomes cannot be painted into the overworld skyblock world (and vice versa). Decide and enforce the rule in `BiomeCommand` and/or `SetBiomeTask` based on `World.Environment` / the target biome's dimension, rejecting mismatches with a localized error.
- [ ] Author the full set of biome rewards against real registered biome keys. Convert the legacy `permission: usb.biome.<key>` grants in `challenges.yml` to the island-scoped `type: biome` reward (or confirm the intended coexistence) and cover the intended biomes from `biomes.yml`, not just the current three.
- [ ] Validate every authored biome key resolves via `Registry.BIOME.match` at load (it already warns; ensure authored keys produce no warnings on a stock server).
- [ ] Integrate the single unmerged commit `65c2dc3b` from `independent-biome-unlocking` (default-unlocked-biomes setting + legacy permission migration) into the 4.0 line, resolving any overlap with the existing default-unlocked-biomes path on the catalog branch (`RuntimeConfig.Biomes#defaultUnlocked()`, consumed in `IslandBiomeUnlocks.unlockedBiomes()` at `IslandBiomeUnlocks.java:42`).
- [ ] Verify the end-to-end flow on a stock install with no permissions plugin: completing a challenge that rewards a biome makes `/is biome <key>` succeed, and resetting the island removes the unlock.
- [ ] Confirm the `usb.biome.<key>` OR-fallback in `canUseBiome` still works for donor ranks/ops after migration.

## References
- Related: #145 (Island-scoped biome unlocking as a first-class challenge reward — do not duplicate).
- Design draft: `docs/challenge-redesign/uskyblock-v2-challenge-redesign.md` (currently untracked / do-not-commit).
- Unmerged work: branch `independent-biome-unlocking`, commit `65c2dc3b`. Note also branch `fix/biome-permission-nodes` exists and may overlap.
- Key files: `uSkyBlock-Core/src/main/resources/biomes.yml`, `uSkyBlock-Core/src/main/resources/challenges.yml`, `.../island/task/SetBiomeTask.java`, `.../command/island/BiomeCommand.java`, `.../biome/BiomeConfig.java`, `.../challenge/IslandBiomeUnlocks.java`, `.../challenge/catalog/ChallengeRewards.java`, `.../challenge/catalog/yaml/ChallengeCatalogYamlParser.java`.

*Category: gameplay-world-code · Effort: medium · Source: 4.0 readiness survey.*

I worked across the consumer-facing reward webview, the campaign CMS, and the ad-ops campaign portal.

Grow ad engagement inside a telecom super-app by making reward-earning simple for end users, while giving marketing teams at multiple telecom providers (Telkomsel and IM3/Indosat) a way to launch and manage campaigns without needing engineering involvement for every change.

Built the consumer-facing webview embedded in the MyIM3 app — users browse offers and coupons, complete them, and claim mobile data vouchers directly back into their telecom account, with deep-linking back into MyIM3/Bima+.

## Goal

On `backend/api`, implement SEP-10 web authentication: a challenge endpoint that returns a Stellar transaction, and a verify endpoint that validates the signed challenge and issues a JWT.

## Context

SEP-10 is the standard auth flow used by every Stellar anchor and most wallet integrations. The Helios wallet uses it to authenticate against the backend (e.g., to subscribe to notifications, to upload encrypted guardian metadata). Indexer and notifications services will all gate on a SEP-10-issued JWT.

Depends on issue **030** (Settings).

## Scope

**Touch:**
- `backend/api/auth/__init__.py` (new)
- `backend/api/auth/sep10.py` (new)
- `backend/api/auth/jwt.py` (new)
- `backend/api/main.py` (mount the auth router)
- `backend/api/tests/test_sep10.py` (new)
- `backend/api/pyproject.toml` (add `pyjwt[crypto]`, `stellar-sdk`)

**Do not touch:**
- Other backend services

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `GET /auth?account=G…` returns `{ transaction, network_passphrase }` per SEP-10 v3
- [ ] Challenge transaction has correct `manageData` op, time bounds, source = server signing key
- [ ] `POST /auth { transaction }` verifies the signed challenge per SEP-10 and returns `{ token: <JWT> }`
- [ ] JWT signed with HS256 (key from settings), claims include `sub` (the authed account), `iat`, `exp` (15 min), `iss` (configurable)
- [ ] Verify rejects: wrong server signature, expired time bounds, invalid client signature, replay (same tx twice)
- [ ] All endpoints validate input with Pydantic; 400 on malformed account, 401 on bad signature
- [ ] `ruff`, `ruff format --check`, `mypy --strict`, `pytest` clean

## Tests required

- Challenge endpoint returns well-formed transaction
- Verify accepts a correctly signed challenge (use stellar-sdk to construct + sign in the test)
- Verify rejects: wrong server sig, expired tx, missing client sig, replay

**Summary:** The 4.0 repeat-economy (Vault currency rewards + unlimited-repeat challenges) is fully modeled in the design but has never actually been played. Before we lock the economy for release, we need a structured beta playtest that validates the specific mob/farm/material throughput gates the design depends on, plus two testplay checkpoints at the mid-game and endgame monument entries. No automated test substitutes for this.

## Why this blocks 4.0

The challenge catalog drives a live economy: rewards grant Vault currency (`RewardApplier.grantCurrency`), challenges repeat without bound by default (`repeatLimit: 0`), and many carry per-repeat rewards. Every required-vs-reward ratio and every "is this even farmable" assumption is currently theoretical. Shipping an untuned economy risks either trivial inflation or unattainable mandatory challenges, both of which are hard to walk back once players have progress. The design draft itself flags drop-rate/throughput assumptions (e.g. wither-skull farming rates, prismarine "scale from guardian farming") that have no in-game confirmation.

## Current state

- The economy is wired end to end: `grantCurrency` is gated on `enableEconomyRewards()` and deposits via the Vault economy hook (`uSkyBlock-Core/src/main/java/us/talabrek/ultimateskyblock/challenge/RewardApplier.java`); the default config enables economy rewards and unlimited repeats (`repeatLimit: 0`).
- The balance itself is unvalidated: the gating challenges (the prismarine monument, the wither-skull beacon chain, the guardian/raid content) carry large hand-in budgets sourced from farms whose real throughput has never been measured on a live island.

## Scope

Validate each of the design's named economy gates against the shipped build:

- [ ] Guardian / elder-guardian drop throughput supplies the mandatory prismarine monument (several thousand prismarine shards) on a real island over a realistic session.
- [ ] Raid-patrol spawning works on a real island (ominous bottles from patrol captains, totems from raids).
- [ ] The guardian-habitat / monument mechanic functions in the Paper per-player world setup.
- [ ] Nether-fortress spawning defaults sustain the wither-skull kill budget — measure skulls/hour vs. the requirement and reconcile the rewards with the design.
- [ ] Audit every reward item and every hand-in against the actually-released build — confirm each item key resolves and each required item is obtainable at that point in progression.
- [ ] Testplay checkpoint 1: play to and through the mid-game tier entry, confirming the economy and unlock gates hold up to that point.
- [ ] Testplay checkpoint 2: play to and through the endgame monument/beacon capstone, confirming the material economy holds at endgame scale.
- [ ] Capture measured throughput numbers and proposed balance adjustments, and feed them back into `challenges.yml` before the economy is locked for release.

## References

- Depends on the `challenges.yml` authoring work and the schematics/monument-material work being in place first (see #128 "4.0 gameplay changes: level progression, scoring, and challenges").
- #145 — island-scoped biome unlocking as a challenge reward (several gated challenges grant biome unlocks).
- #147 — accepted SQLite follow-ups for the 4.0 challenge rework (progress storage underpinning repeats).
- Design draft: `docs/challenge-redesign/uskyblock-v2-challenge-redesign.md` (currently untracked / do-not-commit) — the economy/throughput sections.
- Key files: `uSkyBlock-Core/src/main/resources/challenges.yml`, `uSkyBlock-Core/src/main/java/us/talabrek/ultimateskyblock/challenge/RewardApplier.java`.

*Category: test-release · Effort: large · Source: 4.0 readiness survey.*

## Overview

Implement a daily challenge system that requires players to complete tasks across 2–3 different games. This is the highest-priority cohesion feature for App Store guideline 4.2 compliance (see #1914) — it gives players a reason to open BC Arcade as a product each day, not just a specific game.

## Approach: Deterministic Seeded Generation with Manual Override

Mirror the pattern already used by Daily Word (`GET /daily-word/today?tz_offset_minutes=X`):

- A daily seed derived from the UTC date deterministically selects games and thresholds from a template library
- No cron jobs, no content calendar, no human authoring required for the default path
- The same request on the same day always returns the same challenge
- A database override table allows hand-crafted challenges to be injected for seasonal events without touching code

---

## Backend Spec

### New endpoint

```
GET /daily-challenge/today?tz_offset_minutes=X
```

Response:
```json
{
  "challenge_id": "2026-06-02",
  "title": "The Daily Grind",
  "tasks": [
    { "game": "solitaire", "condition": "complete_game", "threshold": 1, "label": "Complete a Solitaire game" },
    { "game": "starswarm", "condition": "reach_wave", "threshold": 4, "label": "Reach wave 4 in StarSwarm" },
    { "game": "twenty48", "condition": "reach_score", "threshold": 512, "label": "Score 512 in 2048" }
  ],
  "xp_reward": 150,
  "expires_at": "2026-06-03T00:00:00Z"
}
```

### Generation algorithm

1. Seed = `int(date.isoformat().replace("-", ""))` (e.g. 20260602)
2. Use seeded random to pick 2–3 games from the **free game pool** (solitaire, freecell, twenty48, blackjack, mahjong, daily_word) — always include at least 2 free games so premium-gated players aren't blocked
3. For each selected game, pick a condition type from that game's template list (see below)
4. Set thresholds at the ~40th percentile of actual scores from the past 30 days (queried from existing game stats in the DB) — achievable for most players, not trivial
5. Check the override table first; if a row exists for today's date, return it instead

### Template library (starting set)

| Game | Condition | Threshold source |
|---|---|---|
| Solitaire | `complete_game` | binary — 1 completion |
| FreeCell | `complete_game` | binary |
| Twenty48 | `reach_score` | 40th percentile of `final_score` |
| Blackjack | `complete_hand` | N hands (e.g. 3) |
| Blackjack | `end_with_chips` | 40th percentile of `best_chips` |
| Mahjong | `complete_game` | binary |
| StarSwarm | `reach_wave` | 40th percentile of `wave_reached` |
| Sudoku | `complete_puzzle` | binary (any difficulty) |
| Yacht | `complete_game` | binary |
| Sort | `reach_level` | 40th percentile of `level_reached` |
| Daily Word | `complete_puzzle` | binary |

### Override table (PostgreSQL)

```sql
CREATE TABLE daily_challenge_overrides (
    challenge_date DATE PRIMARY KEY,
    payload JSONB NOT NULL,  -- same shape as the generated response
    created_at TIMESTAMPTZ DEFAULT now()
);
```

Inserting a row for a date causes that challenge to be served instead of the generated one. No code deploy needed for seasonal events.

---

## Frontend Spec

### Home screen
- Add a "Daily Challenge" card at the top of the lobby (above the game grid)
- Shows today's tasks, completion state per task (checkmark when done), and XP reward
- Tapping a task deep-links directly into the relevant game

### Challenge completion tracking
- Each game's existing score submission flow (`POST /games/{id}/complete`) should check whether the completed game satisfies any active daily challenge task
- On match, call `POST /daily-challenge/progress` to record task completion
- When all tasks complete, award XP to the player's arcade progression (see #1914)

### Persistence
- Challenge progress cached in AsyncStorage keyed by `challenge_id`
- Flushed to server by SyncWorker when online (same pattern as score queue)

---

## Calibration & Quality Control

- Thresholds are recomputed nightly from the past 30 days of actual game stats — they self-adjust as the player base grows
- Template selection avoids repeating the same game combination within a 30-day rolling window (tracked via seed history, no DB write needed — just check if `seed % N` would produce a recent duplicate)
- Seasonal overrides should be drafted at least 2 weeks ahead so they can be tested before going live

---

## What's Out of Scope

- Premium-only challenge tasks (challenges must always be completable with free games)
- Multiplayer or async challenges (future)
- Leaderboard for challenge completion speed (future — could be Tier 2)

---

## Related

- #1914 — App Store cohesion risk (parent feature)
- #1911 — Unlock/reward system (XP from challenges feeds into this)

## Context

Optional post-release enhancement to **Roguelite Challenge Mode (#79)** — blocked by #79. Inspired by Darkest Dungeon 2's road choices: pick your route from previewed dangers, where the nastier path carries better loot. This addresses the eternal ordeal-RNG complaint (the dreaded Green Dawn) by giving the player agency — as risk-reward, not free convenience.

The game rolls the entire day's ordeal queue up front in `OrdealGenInfo.GenerateOrdeals(day)`, so a Postfix can generate 2-3 candidate queues and present a day-start chooser window (no mid-day modal needed). Each candidate gets a mod-computed danger rating from a maintainable data table; picking the harder slate attaches a completion bounty (LOB, or energy) paid on `OrdealManager.OnOrdealEnd`.

## Player value

Regular players who hate ordeal RNG get agency, but as risk-reward — dodging the scary slate costs the bounty. Challenge-runners always take the bounty; streamers get a chat-vote-friendly decision point.

## Research notes (decompiled source)

- `GenerateOrdeals` is a re-callable public static (candidate slates are trivial to roll); `OnGameInit`/`OnOrdealEnd`/`EnergyModel.AddEnergy` are clean Postfix targets; the deploy phase between `InitGame` and `StartGame` gives a free day-start window for the chooser (vanilla `DeployUI` only shows the max ordeal *level* there, so a preview is additive).
- The slate is never serialized → rewinds just re-present the chooser, with zero save-format risk.
- Writing the private `_ordealList` requires an `I*Internals` reflection adapter in the **Common** NuGet (cross-repo work, per the org rule against raw reflection in mods).

## Open questions

- The chooser must be suppressed on deterministic branches (Kether fixer ordeals, day 50, tutorial, days < 5).
- The danger-rating table is opinionated — make it community-editable so it doesn't go stale.
- Retry-fishing the bounty (rerolling until the hard slate draws a soft type) is a balance nit to mitigate.

## Scope

Medium. Distinct from #139 (forced worst-case, no agency) and #69 (Green Midnight rebalance, not a choice system) — note both in the README.

### Issue #34: Implement Proper Solution Verification in Challenge

**Labels:** `smart-contract`, `priority: high`, `challenge-system`

**Monorepo workspace:** `contract/` — Foundry (Solidity 0.8.28). Run `forge build` and `forge test` from `contract/`.

**Description:**
The current `submitChallengeFlag()` incorrectly compares against the user's own previously stored submission hash rather than the actual solution. The comparison logic needs to verify against the private `solution` variable set by the challenge owner.

**Scope:**
- Fix comparison: `if (_solutionHash == solution)` instead of `submission[msg.sender].solutionHash`
- Add a require that `solution != bytes32(0)` (solution must be set first)
- Store the user's attempt hash for audit trail regardless of correctness

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- [ ] Flag verification checks against owner-set solution
- [ ] Submissions before solution is set are rejected
- [ ] Both correct and incorrect attempts are recorded
- [ ] First correct submission triggers reward

**Files likely affected:**
- `contract/src/core/challenge.sol`

**Pull requests:** Open PRs against `staging` (see [CONTRIBUTING.md](https://github.com/Taida-Debu/zenode/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md)).

### Issue #67: Implement Platform Fee Collection for Reward Distribution

**Labels:** `smart-contract`, `priority: medium`, `token-rewards`

**Monorepo workspace:** `contract/` — Foundry (Solidity 0.8.28). Run `forge build` and `forge test` from `contract/`.

**Description:**
The platform has no fee mechanism to sustain development. Adding a small platform fee on competition prize pools and challenge rewards would fund continued development and staking rewards.

**Scope:**
- Add configurable fee percentage (e.g., 2.5%) to competitions
- Deduct fee during `createCompetition()` USDC deposit
- Route fees to a treasury address (governable)
- Add fee exemption for governance-approved competitions

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- [ ] Platform fee is deducted from prize pool deposits
- [ ] Fee percentage is configurable via governance
- [ ] Fees accumulate in a treasury contract
- [ ] Fee is clearly shown in competition creation events

**Files likely affected:**
- `contract/src/core/competition.sol`
- `contract/src/core/entry.sol`

**Pull requests:** Open PRs against `staging` (see [CONTRIBUTING.md](https://github.com/Taida-Debu/zenode/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md)).

body:
An idea I just had:

Eventually we can have Quests / Challenges (name tentative) that users can make for themselves, and they get rewarded upon completion. These should be small and quick tasks you can easily fit into your day. For example: Do 10 pushups, make your bed, clean your room, do laundry, etc.

Rather than tasks that are Todo list items that users define as things they have to do, quests / challenges are optional things that people should aim to do to build healthy good habits.

When the Social tab is built, I'm thinking users can even share their own challenges and have other people participate in it. A click of a button will add the public quest to your own board, and the owner can see cool stats like how many people took on the quest, completed it, etc.
